items.title: Drones, explosions and soldiers in bulldozers: Surrounded by Israelis in Lebanon's 'model town'
items.description: Dodging the broken glass carpeting her home in southern Lebanon, Mariam al-Yaghi exited onto her upper balcony and pointed. A few hundred metres ​away was a sight the 67-year-old had grown accustomed to: military vehicles moving through the adjacent Lebanese village, still occupied by Israeli troops. Mariam al-Yaghi ,67, Lebanese resident from West Zawtar, stands in her damaged house in southern Lebanon, on October 1, 2026. — Reuters At night, Israeli soldiers patrol so close to Yaghi’s home in ‌West Zawtar that she can hear their voices. By day, she is often trailed by a small Israeli surveillance drone as she toils in her garden. Booms echo throughout the morning as Israel’s military destroys homes in the surrounding occupied towns with controlled detonations and bulldozers. “We hear them all the time from that house over there with the tile roof. We hear their voices yelling, the tanks when they move this way and that way. We hear all of that. They’re very close to us, but we’re sitting here and we’re not scared. Never,” Yaghi told ​ Reuters . Israeli troops withdrew from West Zawtar in July, the first test of a US-backed “pilot zone” plan for Israel to withdraw gradually from southern Lebanon, in exchange for the disarmament of Hezbollah. Damaged homes in West Zawtar, southern Lebanon, on Oct 1, 2026. — Reuters But two months on, ​no further “pilot zones” have been agreed and residents of West Zawtar say their village is no blueprint. In response to questions from Reuters , the Israeli military said work to remove the ⁠threat of Hezbollah’s weapons had not been completed. Drones were used to identify threats, and restrictions on movement of local villagers were intended to protect troops. A US State Department spokesperson said the pilot zone process was “the only viable path” to ​security for both Lebanon and Israel. The zone would expand after the Lebanese army carried out clearance operations in the initial zone, and Hezbollah’s disarmament “is an integral part of this process”. Displaced resident of Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh, Zeinab Loubani, 54, reacts during an interview with Reuters at a school turned into a shelter for displaced families, in Sidon, Lebanon, on July 23, 2026. — Reuters Front-row seat to destruction Beginning seven months ago, more than a million ​Lebanese fled their homes when Israel launched air strikes and a ground invasion in parallel with the war in Iran , after the armed group Hezbollah fired into Israel in solidarity with Tehran. Ending the Lebanon conflict has been an Iranian condition for any peace deal, prompting Washington to press for an accord. But despite months of US-brokered talks between Lebanon and Israel and a ceasefire agreed in June, Israel’s military has continued deadly strikes. Its troops still occupy a self-declared security zone that includes dozens of Lebanese villages, many of which the Israelis have demolished. Residents of West ​Zawtar say their return home in July was bittersweet: they were happy to be back, but found homes in ruins and Israeli troops uncomfortably close. A man walks next to damaged homes in West Zawtar, southern Lebanon, on Oct 1, 2026. — Reuters A tank shell had crashed into the upper floor of Yaghi’s home and all the windows had ​been blown out. Another had pierced her water tank’s roof, turning the water inside blood-red. Repairs will be costly, so Yaghi has delayed them for now. “We’ve put up cardboard and stuff like that because there’s no glass. My other son too, all the glass ‌and everything is ⁠gone. But here we are… until they get the hell out of here,” she said, gesturing towards the Israeli troops in the adjacent village. Few of Yaghi’s neighbours have returned so far, as their homes had been pulverised. Tank tracks ran through her garden, where olive trees she had nurtured for decades lay uprooted. With the harvest beginning, Yaghi was excited to pick whatever remained. Mariam al-Yaghi , 67, Lebanese resident from West Zawtar, stands in her damaged house in southern Lebanon, on Oct 1, 2026. — Reuters People whose groves lie near Israeli troop positions said they were requesting access to their trees through a US-led coordination mechanism between the Lebanese and Israeli militaries. Some mocked the absurdity of asking Washington for permission to pick olives. Others feared approval would come too late for the harvest. Just down the road from West Zawtar lies its twin village, East Zawtar, still occupied ​by Israeli troops who have been systematically demolishing it. ​ Displaced East Zawtar residents came to West Zawtar, where ⁠they sat on white plastic chairs in the main square with a front-row view of their home town across a small valley of olive groves and farmland. One man told Reuters he had seen lights on in his own house over the last three weeks, and expected Israeli troops were laying explosives to detonate it. “You try not to be upset, because it’s happened ​to so many people. But all it takes is one memory from the house, and you break down,” he said. Israeli troops gone, but keeping watch West Zawtar’s mayor, Abed ​Ezzedine, told Reuters the “pilot zone” programme ⁠had not worked, primarily because public services including electricity and running water were still largely unavailable. “In principle, I can tell you that no, it’s not successful. Based on what we were promised: that West Zawtar as a pilot zone would be a model town,” Ezzedine said. Mayor of Zawtar Al-Gharbiyeh, Abed Ezzedin, stands in the outskirts of the village as he waits to return to his hometown, in southern Lebanon, on July 23, 2026. — Reuters Some 70 families had returned, mostly living in corners of their homes that had not been damaged. For many, it was a better option than paying rent elsewhere or living in a displacement shelter. The Lebanese state’s Council for the South has delivered ⁠16 prefabricated houses ​to families whose homes were uninhabitable. But most of the pre-fab dwellings are still unoccupied, with no access to electricity or water. State workers are ​beginning to extend electrical lines, but have had to run them further to a new station, as the village’s old connection ran through East Zawtar. “In a little bit, the drone might fly over people in the town square. It’s not leaving anyone alone,” Ezzedine said. Sure enough, a few moments later, a ​small surveillance drone flew over Ezzedine and a team of Reuters reporters, gradually dropping altitude until it was just a few meters overhead. It hovered for a few minutes, before flying towards the occupied neighbouring village. Header image: A man walks near rubble in West Zawtar, southern Lebanon, October 1, 2026. — Reuters

items.title: LA 2028: Black Queens set for first steps of Olympic Games against Mauritius
items.description: After the underwhelming performance at the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) two months ago, Ghana’s women’s senior national team return to action. The Black Queens will face Mauritius in their first involvement in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games qualifiers. Kim Lars Bjorkegren enjoyed a full house on Wednesday, October 7, after opening camp on Monday ahead of the first leg of the game. Ghana will play as the away team in the first of two meetings between the two sides on Thursday, October 8, with Bjorkegren hoping to start the qualifiers on a good note. Mauritius reached the second round of the qualifiers following their double-header win over Djobouti in the previous round. They claimed a 2-1 victory in the first leg before winning the second leg 1-0. Ghana, on the other hand, was handed a bye in the first round due to their ranking, setting up a clash with Mauritius. Since the introduction of women’s football at the Olympics, Ghana has failed to qualify for all eight editions, as Bjorkegren targets an Olympic appearance. In the qualifiers for the 2024 edition, Ghana fell short in the third round, losing 4-3 on aggregate to Zambia, who eventually got the nod to play at the tournament after beating Morocco in the final phase. The Swedish trainer called up 24 players for the game, with 17 of them part of the WAFCON squad from Morocco, while five players, including Mukarama Abdulai, were making a return to the national team. Two players in Rabiatu Maltiti and Margaret Agyapomaa are new to the setup. Head-to-head Prior to their wins over Djibouti, Mauritius had lost two of their last three games, losing to Botswana and Madagascar in the CASAFA Championship while drawing with Seychelles in the same competition. In that period, they have conceded 12 goals while scoring five goals. Just like Mauritius, Ghana has also won two of their last five games and also lost twice while drawing the other. The Black Queens defeated Cote d’Ivoire and Cape Verde, suffering defeats to Cameroon and Malawi, while drawing with Mali. In the five games, Bjorkegren’s side have scored six goals while shipping in five goals. Where and When? The first leg between Mauritius and Ghana will take place at the Cote d’Or National Sports Complex in St Pierre with kickoff scheduled for 14:30 GMT.

items.title: Mobile services reportedly non-functional in parts of Peshawar ahead of PTI march’s expected arrival
items.description: PESHAWAR: Large parts of the provincial capital reportedly remained without mobile and cellular internet services on Thursday in an unannounced suspension that started last night, Dawn has learnt. The move comes as PTI’s long march, launched on Oct 4 from Lakki Marwat, is set to reach Peshawar today according to PTI’s schedule. The protest march to demand the release of party founder and ex-premier Imran Khan had reached the Khyber district by Wednesday evening. Though there was no word from the provincial government on the unannounced cellular disruption, a Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) official, however, confirmed to Dawn that the authority had ordered the suspension at the directives of higher authorities. The official told Dawn the suspension was temporary and taken as a security precaution during the long march. The official said the ministry orders were conveyed on Wednesday night. Special Assistant to the Chief Minister on Home and Tribal Affairs Tariq Saeed Marwat did not respond to whether his department requested the interior ministry cell phone service suspension. KP Information Minister Shafi Jan was also not available for comment. Meanwhile, some major private schools across Peshawar also remained closed on Thursday. However, government schools, colleges and universities remained open. Many parents found out about the school closure on Thursday morning when their children returned home after finding the school gates locked. Yousaf Khan, a resident of Ring Road, told Dawn that he found out on Thursday morning. “My children were told at the school gate to go back,” he said, adding that he did not hear about the closure due to the suspension of cellular service. “Due to the prevailing political situation in the city, the school will remain closed tomorrow, i.e, on Oct 8”, a notice from one of the private schools read, adding that classes will resume from Friday. However, Private Schools Regulatory Authority (PSRA) officials said no order for school closure was issued, and action will be taken against schools that remained closed without government directions. The authority has also written to the principals of all private schools, stating that certain private educational institutions had been closed by their respective administrations in connection with the ongoing long march, without any notification from the PSRA. “In view of the above, all heads/principals/administrators of private educational institutions are hereby directed to keep their respective institutions open and ensure regular academic activities until clear directions/notification are issued by this authority,” the letter, seen by Dawn , read. It said that failure to comply with the directions would be viewed seriously, and strict disciplinary action would be initiated against the concerned institution/management under the relevant rules and regulations. PTI’s march began from Lakki Marwat on Oct 4, from where the protesters trekked to Kohat on the second day and arrived in Mattani, located on the outskirts of Peshawar, that night. While the plan for the trek after Oct 8 is yet to be announced, the PTI previously announced Islamabad as its final destination. The Centre has warned the party against any protests or gatherings in Islamabad. However, the PTI decided to embark on the march after weekend talks with the federal government failed to bridge their differences for multiple reasons , particularly over the counterterrorism policy.

items.title: Lecornu jette de l’huile sur le feu dans les lycées
items.description: Le 7 octobre au soir, le Premier ministre Sebastien Lecornu a tente d'apaiser la revolte lyceenne lors d'une allocution depuis Matignon. Reconnaissant que « la colere des jeunes ne vient pas de nulle part », il a promis des decisions fin octobre et un « temps de democratie interne » dans les etablissements. Mobilisation lycéenne: "Les premières décisions du gouvernement seront présentées à la fin du mois d'octobre", annonce Sébastien Lecornu https://t.co/A8jYx9xB83 — BFM (@BFMTV) October 7, 2026 Mais aucune mesure d'urgence sur les moyens n'a ete devoilee, Lecornu renvoyant au budget de novembre, un dossier par ailleurs sensible pour le gouvernement . Une « copie blanche » qui attise les tensions La secretaire generale du Syndicat national des enseignements de second degre (Snes-FSU) Sophie Venetitay a fustige cette « copie blanche ». « Sebastien Lecornu essaye clairement de gagner du temps […] c'est quelque part jouer le pourrissement », a-t-elle regrette sur franceinfo, pointant l'absence de signaux concrets comme le reemploi des contractuels ou l'annulation de suppressions de postes. Les chefs d'etablissement, via le Syndicat national des personnels de direction de l'education nationale (SNPDEN-Unsa), ont refuse d'organiser immediatement ces temps d'echange, juges « maladroits » et « hors sol ». Le Snes-FSU appelle par ailleurs a la poursuite de la mobilisation, notamment pour l'acte IV du 8 octobre. 🚨🇫🇷 BREAKING — STRIKE! French education unions back students! Vénétitay, SNES-FSU secretary-general: “What seems important to us is not to stop at yesterday when it comes to supporting high school students. That is why tomorrow, we will still be at their side in support.” https://t.co/HkGSiTh0ls — Pamphlets (@PamphletsY) October 7, 2026 Les oppositions de gauche ont abonde dans ce sens. Manuel Bompard, de La France insoumise (LFI), a tonne que Lecornu etait « incapable d'annoncer une seule mesure concrete », tandis que Marine Tondelier a denonce une strategie visant « l'essoufflement du mouvement » avant les vacances de Toussaint. Ce soir, Lecornu est incapable d’annoncer une seule mesure concrète pour répondre à la colère lycéenne. Soutien aux lycéens et aux étudiants qui appellent à manifester demain dans toute la France et à Paris sur la place de la Bastille à 15h. — Manuel Bompard (@mbompard) October 7, 2026 Ce 8 octobre, pour l'« acte IV » de la mobilisation, les lyceens et etudiants sont de nouveau dans la rue, soutenus par une intersyndicale (FSU, CGT, FO, Sud, Unsa) qui appelle a la greve. Selon le ministere de l'education nationale, 375 etablissements connaissent une suspension totale ou partielle des cours, en baisse de 30 % par rapport a la veille, mais les organisations maintiennent la pression. « Rien ne nous arretera tant qu'il n'y aura pas 10 milliards d'euros sur la table », martele l'Union syndicale lyceenne. Les rassemblements se multiplient, de Paris a Montpellier, dans un climat ou les annonces de Matignon, loin d'eteindre le feu, semblent l'alimenter.

items.title: France : des travailleurs marocains affirment avoir été «esclavagisés» dans des vergers du Gard
items.description: a la barre du tribunal de Nîmes, le 6 octobre, Abderrahim B. a resume la situation en quelques mots : « J'ai dû payer pour travailler. » Comme 14 autres ouvriers marocains, ce saisonnier affirme avoir verse 12 000 euros en liquide a son recruteur, Hamid B., pour obtenir un contrat de travail dans deux exploitations agricoles du Gard, dans le sud de la France. Le recruteur lui aurait promis un salaire mensuel de 2 500 euros et la possibilite de gagner suffisamment d'argent pour ameliorer sa situation. Mais, selon les plaignants, les remunerations finalement percues ne correspondaient pas aux montants annonces ni au nombre d'heures effectuees. Un inspecteur du travail a l'origine de l'alerte a decrit a l'audience une pratique connue dans certains reseaux de recrutement : des contrats seraient proposes a des travailleurs marocains contre plusieurs milliers d'euros. « C'est un secret de polichinelle que des contrats de travail se vendent 8 000 a 15 000 euros pour des Marocains », a-t-il declare. Des conditions de travail et de logement degradees Selon les enqueteurs, le systeme aurait fonctionne pendant au moins trois ans. Les travailleurs etaient recrutes au Maroc par Hamid B. et son epouse Nazia K., qui s'occupait notamment des demarches administratives. Apres le versement de ce que les plaignants decrivent comme un « ticket d'entree » de 12 000 euros, les ouvriers auraient ete prives de leurs documents d'identite. Ils auraient ensuite ete loges pour environ 150 euros par mois dans des chambres depourvues de mobilier et d'eau chaude. Certains auraient meme dû dormir a meme le sol, faute de lits suffisants. Les travailleurs indiquent egalement avoir effectue de longues journees, parfois jusqu'a 13 heures, sans que les heures supplementaires soient remunerees comme telles. Une video versee au dossier montre des ouvriers travaillant de nuit sous un orage, sans equipement adapte. Selon les parties civiles, le systeme prevoyait en outre de nouveaux paiements pour ceux qui souhaitaient revenir travailler la saison suivante. Les prevenus contestent les accusations Le couple de recruteurs est poursuivi pour traite d'etres humains, aux cotes d'un dirigeant d'exploitation agricole. Un second exploitant du Gard comparaît, entre autres, pour des faits de travail dissimule. Devant le tribunal, Hamid B. a rejete les accusations, se presentant comme un simple ouvrier qui soutient ne savoir « ni lire ni ecrire ». Interroge sur des videos montrant des travailleurs recrutes participant a des travaux autour de sa piscine, il a assure qu'ils avaient ete realises a des fins de promotion sur les reseaux sociaux. Il a par ailleurs conteste la signification de sequences dans lesquelles il apparaît en train de compter des liasses de billets, parlant d'un « piege pour les reseaux sociaux ». Avec son epouse, il a explique que les sommes deposees en liquide ou par cheque sur leurs comptes correspondaient a leurs economies ou a des dons familiaux. L'exploitant Geoffrey M., qui produit notamment des cerises, des abricots, des grenades et des kakis, a pour sa part reconnu qu'Hamid B. lui « trouvait des employes », tout en affirmant ne pas avoir connaissance de leurs conditions de logement ni d'eventuels paiements pour l'obtention des contrats. Il a evoque les difficultes rencontrees par le secteur agricole pour recruter de la main-d'œuvre : « Comment on fait, sinon ? ». Jusqu'a 18 mois de prison avec sursis requis Les 15 travailleurs marocains avaient donne l'alerte a la suite d'une inspection du travail. Leurs avocats ont salue leur « courage » pour avoir denonce des conditions qu'ils qualifient d'« esclaves modernes ». La Confederation paysanne, elle aussi partie civile, a denonce une situation qu'elle considere comme revelatrice de violences systemiques visant des travailleurs etrangers et a appele a renforcer la lutte contre l'exploitation des personnes immigrees. La procureure Nathalie Welte a estime que l'infraction de traite d'etres humains etait constituee pour trois des quatre prevenus. Elle a requis a leur encontre des peines allant d'un an a 18 mois de prison avec sursis, ainsi que des amendes comprises entre 50 000 et 150 000 euros. a l'audience, la magistrate a resume les conditions decrites par les victimes : « Pas d'eau, pas de toilette, pas de vestiaire, on travaille 13 heures par jour dans un champ, et en plus on paye pour ca », faisant aussi etat de brimades, d'insultes, d'humiliations et de cris d'animaux. Le tribunal de Nîmes doit desormais mettre l'affaire en delibere. Les dossiers concernant l'exploitation de travailleurs etrangers dans les secteurs agricoles du Gard et du Vaucluse sont regulierement portes devant la justice francaise. Des procedures similaires ont aussi emerge ces dernieres annees dans le vignoble bordelais.

items.title: Christa Pike now walking after failed US execution, lawyer tells BBC
items.description: Christa Pike is “up and walking” while in hospital after last week’s botched attempt to execute her in the US state of Tennessee, a member of her legal team says. Pike, 50, who was sentenced to death after murdering Colleen Slemmer with her then-boyfriend in 1995, survived two lethal injections on 30 September. Experts described it as unprecedented. Speaking late on Wednesday to BBC Radio 4’s Today programme, lawyer Stephen Ferrell said he had not spoken to Pike directly but that he had learned she was moving around her hospital room for the first time while still being mentally “foggy”. Earlier, a court ordered the state of Tennessee to preserve all evidence related to the failed execution. That evidence could lay the groundwork for a future lawsuit against the state. The Pike case is now in uncharted territory, as Pike is believed to be the only person to have survived an execution attempt by lethal injection. The failed execution was branded a “mess” by the mother of Slemmer, who was among those pushing for Pike to be put to death. Pike’s boyfriend at the time of Slemmer’s gruesome murder, Tadaryl Shipp, was spared the death penalty because he was not legally an adult when the crime was committed. He remains in prison. Pike was 18 and Shipp was 17 when they beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for troubled teens. In their updates on Pike’s condition after the attempted execution, her team had previously said she was awake and speaking, and experiencing anger and confusion. She was said at that stage to be handcuffed to her bed. In the latest updates, given to the BBC, Ferrell said Pike was continuing to experience the after-effects of the drug pentobarbital, which was injected into her body in two doses by prison staff during the scheduled execution on 30 September. Once it became clear that Pike was not going to die, she was taken to hospital, where she was initially unconscious and declared to be in a critical condition. As of late on Tuesday, though, she was “fairly well”, Ferrell told the BBC. “What’s been described to me is that physically there’s quite a bit going on, that her arms are very injured and she’s not able to use them very much.” Of her physical movements, he added: “She is up and walking for the first time today, but just around the room, not very far.” Turning to her mental state, he said: “I think it’s kind of good and bad. Good that she is fairly with it, but she’s also somewhat foggy. She can lose her train of thought really easily and forgets where she’s going.” Ferrell said much remained unknown about what happens next. “I assume [the situation for Pike] will keep improving, but there could be some permanent damage. We don’t know that yet.” He added that the team wanted Pike to receive psychological support, since that “clearly is necessary now”. Ferrell and his colleagues – who highlighted ahead of the attempted execution that Pike had a condition that would make the injection method difficult – oppose any new attempt by state prison authorities to follow the same approach. They are also calling on the state governor, Bill Lee, to downgrade Pike’s punishment to the lesser sentence of life in prison without parole. Meanwhile, Tennessee’s proponents of capital punishment have suggested that a different method be used. Senator Marsha Blackburn, the Republican candidate for state governor in next month’s election, said: “Bring back the electric chair.” Asked during a court hearing on Wednesday whether the state intended to reschedule Pike’s execution, the state’s attorney general said he did not know. For now, Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has ordered a pause on all executions in the state for the rest of the year, and has said he wants answers about what went wrong. The state’s prisons chief is resigning after the failed execution. Wednesday’s court hearing related to the preservation of evidence following the first attempt. The judge, I’Ashea Myles, ordered that “anything that was in the actual room needs to be preserved and maintained,” including IV lines and syringes, as well as waste, like packaging, inserts, and labels. The judge also demanded documentation on Pike’s psychological condition prior to, during and after the 30 September execution attempt. She advised the state to take “special care” not to misplace or accidentally delete any information that may be pertinent to the case.

items.title: Minister appeals to NASWDEN to suspend industrial action.
items.description: …as FG targets 10 mm annual steel production by 2030 By Gabriel Ewepu, Abuja The Minister of Steel Development, Prince Abubakar Audu, on Wednesday, appealed to the leadership of the National Association of Scrap and Waste Dealers Employers of Nigeria, NASWDEN, to suspend its ongoing industrial action. As contained in a statement signed by the Head, Press & Public Relations Department, Tine-Iulun Maureen, Audu made the call through the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry, Ambassador Nura Abba Rimi, to the leadership of NASWDEN to suspend the strike. According to the statement, the minister said in the interest of industrial harmony, mutual understanding and the overall stability and development of Nigeria’s steel sector, the strike should be suspended. Meanwhile, the statement highlighted reasons by the workers for embarking on the strike, which include alleged undervaluation of scrap metals, weight reductions arising from malpractices involving weighing scales, the involvement of local and other steel-producing companies in direct scrap metals trading, the importation of billets, and other practices perceived by the Association to be limiting the effective participation of local scrap dealers in the steel value chain. The Ministry says it recognises the seriousness and importance of these concerns and is currently giving them due consideration in consultation with the National Steel Council, with a view to developing practical, balanced and sustainable institutional measures to address the issues raised. “In furtherance of this process, the Honourable Minister has directed the Permanent Secretary, in collaboration with the Office of the Executive Secretary of the National Steel Council, to invite the apex leadership of NASWDEN for further discussions and effective mediation on the issues raised by the Association, as well as their implications for steel-producing companies and other operators within the sector. “The Honourable Minister urges NASWDEN and all stakeholders within the steel industry, particularly steel-producing companies, to cooperate fully and uphold their respective obligations. All parties are expected to embrace dialogue, good faith and responsible engagements in the resolution of these issues affecting the sector. “The Minister further calls on all stakeholders to recognise the significant efforts and policy direction of His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, towards repositioning and developing Nigeria’s steel sector under the Renewed Hope Agenda. The Federal Government remains committed to creating an enabling environment for investments, increased domestic production, local participation and sustainable growth across the steel value chain. “The Honourable Minister emphasises that the development of a strong and competitive domestic steel industry requires the collective commitment and cooperation of all stakeholders. No individual or group interest should undermine the broader national objective of building a viable steel industry capable of supporting Nigeria’s industrialisation and economic transformation. “The collective efforts of all stakeholders are essential to achieving the Federal Government’s target of 10 million metric tonnes of annual steel production by 2030, while strengthening local value addition, creating employment opportunities and reducing Nigeria’s dependence on imported steel products. “The Honourable Minister therefore calls on NASWDEN to sheathe its sword, suspend the ongoing industrial action and return to the negotiation table, while assuring the Association and all stakeholders of the Ministry’s readiness to facilitate constructive engagement towards resolving the issues raised. “The Ministry of Steel Development remains committed to ensuring a fair, stable and conducive operating environment for all legitimate stakeholders in the steel sector and will continue to engage relevant parties towards the sustainable development of Nigeria’s steel industry.” The post Minister appeals to NASWDEN to suspend industrial action. appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Maricarmen y las elecciones del 29-N, en directo | El PP veta los minutos de silencio por Maricarmen en el Senado, el Ayuntamiento y la Asamblea de Madrid
items.description: Ni el Ayuntamiento de Madrid ni la Asamblea han guardado este jueves un minuto de silencio por la muerte de Maricarmen . El grupo municipal de Más Madrid propuso poco después de conocerse el fallecimiento un minuto de silencio fuera del Palacio de Cibeles, sede del Consistorio madrileño, antes del pleno extraordinario que se celebra hoy precisamente para tratar cuestiones relacionadas con la vivienda. A última hora del día, ni PP ni Vox habían respondido a la petición hecha a la Junta de Portavoces. El miércoles, el PP ya vetó un minuto de silencio por Maricarmen en la Asamblea de Madrid. Más Madrid y PSOE, por su parte, han guardado un minuto de silencio, fuera y dentro del Ayuntamiento, así como en el patio de la Asamblea. Les Corts Valencianes también han homenajeado a la anciana, pero el grupo parlamentario de Vox se ha ausentado durante el reconocimiento. El PSOE ha pedido en la Diputación Permanente del Senado un minuto de silencio por Maricarmen y el presidente de la Cámara Alta, Pedro Rollán, lo ha denegado por no existir precedentes, si bien ha mostrado la solidaridad con la familia. US and Lebanon protecting wanted Syrian general, BBC finds
items.description: A former Syrian general wanted for crimes against humanity is being bankrolled and protected by the US and Lebanese authorities, a BBC News investigation has found. Bassam al-Hassan, who oversaw Syria’s chemical weapons programme and was a senior adviser to former President Bashar al-Assad, is being harboured in Lebanon following the Assad regime’s collapse in 2024. An investigation by the BBC and the US broadcaster NPR has discovered that Hassan has been allowed to remain there under an arrangement involving the FBI, and other US and Lebanese authorities. This is because of his willingness to provide information about the abduction of American journalist Austin Tice in Syria in 2012, as well as additional intelligence, we have been told. Last month the BBC revealed Tice’s abduction had been a planned operation, with Hassan in the chain of command. Officials from two different branches of Syria’s new government have told the BBC they want Hassan returned to face trial, but that US authorities want him kept in Lebanon, and they say there is little Damascus can do about this. We asked the FBI, the CIA and Lebanon’s General Directorate of General Security to comment on our findings. Only the FBI responded, declining to comment and instead directing us to a past statement that said its focus remained on establishing the facts around the Tice case and securing his return. In response to our findings, Phil Elwood, spokesperson for the Tice family said: “If what you are saying is true, the fact that our tax dollars are being used to furnish a comfortable life for someone associated with the use of chemical weapons on Syrian civilians, who claims to have had Austin Tice executed, is offensive. “This is nothing less than aiding and abetting the escape of a wanted war criminal. The Syrians deserve justice and he should be returned to stand trial.” ADVERTISING As part of a years-long investigation featured in the new BBC podcast: Where is Austin Tice? the BBC has reviewed a detailed record of a meeting between Hassan, FBI and CIA representatives, and Lebanese security officials, where Tice’s case is discussed. In it, Hassan is offered “residency”, “protection” and help securing his “living needs” in return for information, primarily about Tice. Sources with knowledge of the arrangement confirmed this was the case, and described to us how Hassan receives money from the US authorities through an intermediary, making it harder to trace. Hassan is sanctioned by the US government. Yet people connected to the Tice investigation say they have seen little evidence it has significantly advanced since Hassan began providing information as part of this agreement. The deal is believed to have been struck in the spring of 2025. Sources with knowledge of the investigation have expressed concerns that Hassan’s arrangement with the US could continue indefinitely, at significant expense but with little gain. Hassan is not the only Syrian regime official whose connection to the Tice case has seemingly afforded him financial payments or assistance for living abroad. One former regime member said he had received money from the FBI multiple times in exchange for his co-operation on Tice’s case. It was “not in his interest to share all the information all at once,” he told the BBC, “in order to be able to drag out how long he can continue to receive payments from them [the US authorities]”. Another former regime member connected to the Tice case claimed he was living in Lebanon under the “patronage” of the US authorities, citing this as the reason he could not speak to us about Tice. The BBC spoke to a former senior Lebanese intelligence official who confirmed that Lebanese intelligence does have arrangements with the Americans, and that these types of payments have and do take place when both agencies have overlap in cases, but said he had no knowledge of payments involving the Tice case. Following the fall of the Assad regime in early December 2024, Hassan is believed to have initially escaped to Iran. A Syrian businessman, with strong connections to both the former regime and the Lebanese authorities, told the BBC that negotiations had then taken place – involving the US, Lebanon, and Iran – to bring Hassan to Lebanon. The businessman, who asked to remain anonymous, said Hassan was valuable, not only because of what he is believed to know about Tice, but because of his knowledge of Syria’s chemical weapons programme and its military relationship with Iran – secrets that US intelligence was allegedly interested in. Hassan told US investigators last year that Tice had been executed on former President Assad’s orders, but several people with knowledge of the investigation have questioned the details of his account. Hassan has provided a potential location for Tice’s remains, but when the site was searched, nothing was found – according to multiple sources familiar with the dig – casting doubt on the validity of some of Hassan’s information. There are questions, however, over how thoroughly the site was searched. Two sources who said they had intimate knowledge of the operation told the BBC that US authorities stopped digging before the search had been completed, possibly because of security concerns. When the BBC managed to reach Hassan by phone last year to ask for an interview, he directed us to seek permission for him to speak from the FBI and CIA at the US embassy in Beirut. Our investigation has found that other Syrian officials connected to the Tice case have also apparently found refuge abroad. They include Mohammad Makhlouf, who reported to Hassan in Syria and was connected to Tice’s detention – now believed to be residing in Lebanon. And Sakr Rustom, Hassan’s nephew who was involved in Tice’s abduction, now believed to be moving between the UAE and Lebanon. When the BBC attempted to speak to Rustom about Tice’s case, he said he “preferred to focus on matters of the future”. Ghassan Nassour, a former general in Syria’s Republican Guard, is said by former members of the National Defence Forces to have presided over the jail Tice was held in, and is believed to be living in the UAE with his family, we have been told.

items.title: 2027: Don’t insult my opponents — Onjeh
items.description: The 2027 Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Benue South Senatorial candidate, Daniel Onjeh, has appealed to his supporters, particularly young people, not to insult or attack his political opponents on his behalf ahead of the general elections. Onjeh, a former Chairman of the Governing Board of the Projects Development Institute (PRODA), Enugu, said political differences should not turn brothers and sisters into enemies, urging his supporters to focus on issues, records and ideas rather than personal attacks. He made the appeal while sharing photographs of himself separately with former Senate President, Senator David Mark, and Senate Minority Leader, Senator Abba Moro, both of whom he had contested against at different times. According to him, he deliberately shared the photographs to demonstrate the importance of political tolerance, forgiveness and maintaining relationships beyond elections. “I contested against Senator David Mark, and afterwards, we could still sit together. I contested against Senator Abba Moro, and afterwards, we could still sit together. They did not come to me; I went to them,” Onjeh said. He urged his supporters to avoid responding to provocations from opponents, insisting that those who believe in his political principles should promote his record and ideas instead. “As we prepare to commence our campaigns in the coming days, I want to make this very clear to everyone who believes in me: nobody should insult any of my opponents because of me. Nobody,” he said. “If you believe in my principles and what I stand for, talk about the issues. Talk about my record, my ideas and what I propose to do differently.” Onjeh recalled that an overzealous supporter of one of his opponents had once insulted his late mother during the heated 2016 Benue South senatorial rerun election. He said despite being deeply hurt by the incident, he refused to retaliate. “If there was anything capable of provoking me beyond measure, it was someone insulting my late mother. But I did not react. I am not asking my supporters to do something I have not practised myself,” he said. He also recalled being falsely accused on social media of being HIV-positive, saying he chose to clear his name with evidence rather than trade insults with the person behind the allegation. Onjeh said the experience reinforced his belief in forgiveness and the need to separate political disagreements from personal relationships. “Some people have misunderstood my firmness on matters of principle for stubbornness. But disagreement is not disrespect,” he said. He also recounted his legal battle with Moro following the 2023 Benue South senatorial election, which progressed from the Election Petition Tribunal to the Court of Appeal. According to him, he rejected an approach by Moro to settle the matter outside court because he believed that doing so would compromise the trust placed in him by his supporters. “I told Senator Moro that I would rather lose the case in court than sit at a table and compromise what I believed in,” he said. Although the final judgment went against him, Onjeh said he later visited Moro, maintaining that political disagreement should not become personal enmity. “Elections will come and go. Political platforms may change. Offices will change hands. But we will remain sons and daughters of the same Benue South,” he said. Onjeh urged younger people in the senatorial district not to inherit political divisions from previous generations, saying candidates should present their records and proposals and allow voters to decide. “There is no need for hatred. There is no need for insults,” he said. “But don’t insult anyone because of me. And don’t inherit another person’s political disagreement as your personal war.” The post 2027: Don’t insult my opponents — Onjeh appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: MTTD records 2,151 road deaths in 10,157 crashes between January and September
items.description: The Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) says 2,151 people have died in road crashes recorded across Ghana between January and September 2026. A further 12,230 people sustained various degrees of injuries during the period, highlighting the continued toll of road crashes on lives and livelihoods across the country. According to the MTTD, a total of 10,157 road crashes were recorded within the first nine months of the year, involving 17,197 vehicles. Director of Education, Research and Training at the MTTD, ACP Alexander Kwaku Obeng, disclosed the figures in an interview on Thursday, October 8. He said the data covered road crashes reported to the Police across all 25 police regions in the country. ACP Obeng said police investigators were deployed to various crash scenes to assist victims and support emergency efforts, particularly in cases where people were trapped in vehicles. “I have with me data from January to September 2026. These are crashes that have been reported to us in our 25 police regions, and police investigators have responded to support Ghanaians who were trapped in these preventable crashes. “10,157 crashes were recorded involving 17,197 vehicles. Sustained injuries were also 12,230, and persons who lost their lives in these preventable crashes were 2,151.” ACP Obeng stressed the need for motorists and other road users to exercise greater caution and adhere to road safety regulations to help reduce the number of crashes and fatalities on Ghana’s roads.

items.title: Most UK diplomats to leave East Jerusalem consulate, Israel says, as Miliband says ‘vital services’ to rema
items.description: Most diplomats will leave the British consulate in occupied East Jerusalem, Israel says, but the UK insists the building “will not be closing”, and will operate as a “UK Mission”. “We did not want it to come to this,” Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar wrote on social media, as he said 20 diplomats and the consul general would leave Israel while a task force of seven could remain in the building “with a very limited scope of activity”. UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband responded that some staff had been “temporarily withdrawn” for security reasons, but stressed the mission will “work with the Palestinian people”. Israel said in September it would shut the consulate, in retaliation for UK sanctions on Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank which are illegal under international law. The UK government had made last-ditch efforts to persuade Israel not to close the British consulate ahead of Thursday’s deadline, after the Israeli government said it would close the consulate within 30 days of the UK sanctions announcement. The consulate, which was first established in 1838, handles UK relations with Palestinians in Jerusalem as well as in the West Bank and Gaza. It is distinct from the UK embassy in Tel Aviv, which is the UK’s main diplomatic hub with Israel. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said the country had implemented measures announced on 8 September in response to UK sanctions. “The British Consulate in Jerusalem is closing its operations today. Accordingly, the sign of the British Consulate in Jerusalem has been removed,” he wrote on social media. However, the British flag could still be seen outside on Thursday morning, and several staff were seen entering. Saar said talks with the UK government had resulted in agreement on certain principles, including that “the consul general and 20 diplomats (including the consul general) are ending their duties and will leave Israel.” But Saar acknowledged that the building is “the property of the British government” and said Israel had authorised “a task force of only seven diplomats with a very limited scope of activity” to operate in the building. As a result of this agreement with the UK, he said, “no steps will be taken against Israel”. Israeli media had been reporting that the UK had threatened to expel Israeli diplomats from London – raising the prospect of further damaging bilateral relations. This agreement is a compromise of sorts and means – for the moment – the heat has been taken out of a dispute that could have further worsened UK-Israel relations. Israel can claim that the British Consulate is “closing its operations”. A score of British diplomats, including the consul general, are leaving. But Miliband says they are going only temporarily and only for their safety and security. He continues to insist Israel has no legal right to close the consulate. “The UK government reiterates its long-standing view that East Jerusalem is occupied territory,” Miliband wrote in a statement. Following discussions with the Israeli government, he said, the building “will not be closing” and will be known as the UK Mission, Jerusalem from Thursday. However Miliband said an understanding had not been reached on “necessary assurances for the security and protections of our staff and premises”. “Accordingly the UK has temporarily withdrawn a number of staff and families to ensure their safety and security,” he added. The Foreign Office said the seven UK diplomats who remain will be “independent and operational” and continue to deliver vital services. Israel said they will provide “only a limited scope of activity”. FCDO sources described the deal as a “good outcome” because the entire operation was not closing, as had been threatened. They said that maintaining a UK presence would help build back the mission in the future. Speaking to the Today programme, Foreign Office minister Stephen Doughty explained: “The building remains open. We retain our presence, we continue having staff able to do important work engaging with the Palestinian Authority… and we are engaging in ongoing conversations with Israel on this matter.” Asked if this was a political fudge, Doughty said “you can see what’s changed in terms of a name but crucially our presence remains”, adding that the “policies towards this Israeli government, which we fundamentally disagree with” would continue. The foreign secretary made clear the UK reserved the right to take what he called “reciprocal action” but said he would not do so while “discussions are under way and credible”. That means any UK retaliation is unlikely before Israel’s elections later this month.

items.title: Finale Maroc-Sénégal : ce que le TAS va examiner aujourd’hui avant de rendre son verdict
items.description: Neuf mois après une finale à rebondissements, le Sénégal et le Maroc se retrouvent devant le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS), à Lausanne. La juridiction sportive examine ce jeudi 8 octobre le recours de la Fédération sénégalaise de football (FSF) contre la décision de la Confédération africaine de football (CAF) ayant retiré aux Lions le titre de la CAN 2025 et attribué la victoire au Maroc sur tapis vert. L’audience se tient à huis clos et aucune décision ne sera rendue ce jeudi. Une finale gagnée sur le terrain, puis perdue sur décision de la CAF Le 18 janvier 2026, au stade Prince Moulay Abdellah de Rabat, le Sénégal et le Maroc disputent la finale de la CAN 2025. Après 90 minutes sans but, la rencontre bascule dans les dernières minutes du temps réglementaire. Après intervention de la VAR, l’arbitre congolais Jean-Jacques Ndala accorde un penalty au Maroc. Les joueurs sénégalais quittent alors momentanément la pelouse pour protester contre cette décision. Après plusieurs minutes d’interruption, ils regagnent le terrain. Brahim Diaz manque finalement le penalty face à Édouard Mendy. La rencontre reprend et se poursuit en prolongation. Trois minutes après le début de la prolongation, Pape Gueye inscrit le but qui permet au Sénégal de s’imposer 1-0. La CAF avait alors officiellement présenté le Sénégal comme champion d’Afrique. L’affaire ne s’arrête pas au coup de sifflet final. Le 17 mars 2026, le Jury d’appel de la CAF, saisi par la Fédération royale marocaine de football, annule la décision disciplinaire précédente et déclare le Sénégal forfait pour la finale, en application des articles 82 et 84 du règlement de la CAN. Le résultat est homologué sur le score de 3-0 en faveur du Maroc, qui devient officiellement selon instance de la CAF champion d’Afrique. Le recours du Sénégal devant le TAS La Fédération sénégalaise de football décide de contester cette décision devant le TAS. L’appel, enregistré le 25 mars 2026, vise l’annulation de la décision de la CAF et demande que le Sénégal soit déclaré vainqueur de la CAN 2025. La procédure a ensuite suivi son cours avec l’échange des mémoires entre les parties. Le litige oppose désormais la FSF à la CAF et à la Fédération royale marocaine de football. Le TAS a fixé l’audience au 8 octobre à Lausanne. Elle se déroule en français, à huis clos, en présence des parties et d’une formation de trois arbitres. Le Tribunal précise qu’à l’issue des débats, les arbitres délibéreront avant de rendre leur sentence à une date qui n’est pas encore connue. Ce que le TAS va réellement examiner L’enjeu ne consiste pas simplement à déterminer quelle équipe avait gagné le match sur le terrain. La formation arbitrale doit examiner la légalité et le bien-fondé de la décision de la CAF au regard des règlements applicables et des faits de la rencontre. Le TAS dispose, dans une procédure d’appel, d’un « plein pouvoir d’examen » sur les faits et le droit. Selon l’article R57 de son Code, il peut soit rendre une nouvelle décision qui remplace celle contestée, soit annuler cette dernière et renvoyer l’affaire à l’instance qui a statué précédemment. Cela signifie que plusieurs issues sont juridiquement envisageables : confirmer la décision de la CAF, l’annuler et rétablir le résultat sportif, modifier la sanction ou encore renvoyer le dossier devant l’instance compétente. Une jurisprudence qui ne donne pas de réponse toute faite La difficulté du dossier tient notamment à l’absence d’un précédent parfaitement identique. Les affaires évoquées ces dernières années présentent des similitudes, mais aussi des différences importantes. En réalité, aucune situation antérieure ne présente exactement les mêmes caractéristiques que la finale Maroc-Sénégal Le dossier Wydad-Espérance de Tunis, en 2019, constitue néanmoins l’un des précédents les plus proches. Lors de la finale retour de la Ligue des champions africaine, le Wydad avait refusé de reprendre le match après une interruption. Le TAS avait considéré que ce refus constituait un abandon au sens du règlement disciplinaire de la CAF et avait confirmé le principe de la défaite par forfait. Mais le contexte était différent. Dans cette affaire, le Wydad n’avait pas repris le jeu après une longue interruption liée notamment à un problème de VAR et à des contestations. Le TAS avait estimé que les conditions de reprise étaient réunies et que le refus de poursuivre la rencontre engageait la responsabilité du club. Autre élément important : dans sa sentence de 2020, le TAS avait annulé une décision du Comité exécutif de la CAF pour des raisons procédurales, tout en permettant à l’Espérance de conserver le trophée. Ce dossier montre donc que le Tribunal peut distinguer la question du résultat sportif de celle de la régularité de la décision prise par l’instance dirigeante. Une affaire sans précédent totalement comparable C’est précisément ce qui rend le dossier Maroc-Sénégal difficile à anticiper. Le Sénégal a quitté la pelouse, mais est revenu quelques minutes plus tard. Le match a ensuite repris normalement, le penalty a été manqué et la rencontre s’est poursuivie jusqu’à son terme, avec une victoire sénégalaise en prolongation (1-0 a.p) et le trophée remis au vainqueur. Dans l’affaire Wydad-Espérance, au contraire, l’équipe qui avait quitté la pelouse n’était finalement pas revenue poursuivre le match. Le TAS avait alors retenu l’abandon de la rencontre. Cette différence pourrait être au cœur de l’argumentation devant la formation arbitrale. La question sera donc notamment de déterminer si le fait d’avoir momentanément quitté la pelouse, avant de revenir et de terminer la rencontre, peut juridiquement être assimilé à un abandon au sens des règlements de la CAF. Le verdict ne sera pas connu aujourd’hui Contrairement à ce que pourraient laisser penser certaines informations circulant sur les réseaux sociaux, l’audience du 8 octobre ne débouchera pas immédiatement sur un verdict. Le TAS a clairement indiqué qu’il ne pouvait pas annoncer la date de sa décision et que celle-ci ne serait pas prononcée le jour de l’audience. La formation arbitrale doit d’abord délibérer après avoir entendu les arguments des différentes parties. Le droit procédural du TAS lui permet ensuite de rendre une nouvelle décision se substituant à celle de la CAF ou d’annuler cette décision et de renvoyer le dossier à l’instance compétente. Dans l’attente de cette sentence, la décision de la CAF reste donc la décision en vigueur : le Maroc demeure officiellement champion de la CAN 2025. Trois scénarios principaux Premier scénario : le TAS confirme la décision de la CAF. Le Maroc conserverait alors officiellement le titre attribué sur tapis vert et le résultat de la finale resterait homologué à 3-0. Deuxième scénario : le TAS donne raison au Sénégal. Il pourrait annuler la décision de la CAF et, dans le cadre de son pouvoir de pleine juridiction, rendre une nouvelle décision rétablissant le résultat obtenu sur le terrain. Le Sénégal retrouverait alors officiellement le titre remporté le 18 janvier. Troisième scénario : le TAS renvoie l’affaire. Le Tribunal peut également annuler la décision contestée et renvoyer le dossier devant l’instance ayant statué en dernier afin qu’elle statue à nouveau, conformément à l’analyse juridique du TAS. Pour l’heure, aucune de ces issues ne peut être considérée comme acquise. La jurisprudence montre que le TAS examine les faits, les règlements applicables et les circonstances précises de chaque affaire. Dans le dossier Maroc-Sénégal, l’élément central sera donc moins la comparaison mécanique avec les précédents que l’interprétation des règles de la CAF à la lumière de ce qui s’est réellement passé à Rabat. Après neuf mois de procédure, la finale de la CAN 2025 entre ainsi dans sa dernière phase judiciaire. Mais le dernier mot n’est pas encore connu : le verdict viendra après l’audience de Lausanne, à une date que le TAS n’a pas encore fixée. C.G. DIOP

items.title: Ghana needs 150,000 more tonnes of palm oil annually to meet demand – OPDAG
items.description: Ghana’s annual crude palm oil production falls short of domestic demand by an estimated 150,000 metric tonnes, prompting calls for increased investment in farming and processing. The President of the Oil Palm Development Association of Ghana (OPDAG), Paul Kwabena Amaning, said the country produces approximately 250,000 metric tonnes annually, compared with demand of about 400,000 metric tonnes. Speaking at a one-day workshop for stakeholders in the oil palm sector, he described the deficit as an opportunity to increase domestic output, upgrade processing operations and make the industry more competitive. The workshop examined financing and the role of digital financial services across the oil palm value chain. Mr Amaning said Ghana has an estimated 360,000 hectares under oil palm cultivation, with the industry supporting approximately 631,000 people. He noted that the proposed US$500 million financing for oil palm development could help tackle barriers to growth. However, he urged stakeholders to ensure that funding arrangements accommodate smallholder farmers, aggregators and artisanal processors. “As OPDAG President, I consider the inclusion of these small operators particularly important,” he said. He explained that artisanal processors make substantial contributions to palm oil production, rural employment and economic activity, but struggle to obtain affordable credit, modern machinery and formal business support. Mr Amaning also called for greater use of digital financial services to facilitate payments and improve business operations among farmers, processors, traders, transporters and exporters. “Digital financial services can help improve payment security, strengthen record-keeping, increase transparency, and create opportunities for businesses to access savings, credit, insurance and other financial products,” he said. He stressed that successful digitalisation would require more than transferring payments to mobile platforms. Reliable connectivity, reasonable transaction fees, accessible payment agents and systems that work across different platforms would be essential. Consumer protection and practical training, he added, would also help users build confidence in digital services. Mr Amaning said digital transaction records could enable financial institutions to better assess small businesses and their funding needs, provided appropriate consent and safeguards were in place. He further identified the sector’s developing traceability and revenue assurance system as a potential means of improving industry records and supporting access to finance. He called for closer cooperation among government agencies, banks, financial technology companies, mobile network operators, mills, buyers and industry associations. “Policies and financial solutions will be more effective when voices of farmers, processors, and other industry participants are heard and reflected in their design,” he said.

items.title: Renforcement des systèmes de santé : plaidoyer pour l’utilisation des compétences disponibles
items.description: L’utilisation des compétences disponibles devrait permettre de renforcer les systèmes de santé. C’est l’avis du Dr Oumar Sagna, conseiller technique du Directeur général de la santé (Dgs). Depuis novembre 2022, Enda santé met en œuvre au Sénégal, au Burkina Faso et en République démocratique du Congo (Rdc) le projet « Healthcare worker professional associations (Hpa) », avec l'appui de la Fondation Gates. Celui-ci vise à renforcer les systèmes de santé à travers l'accompagnement des associations de professionnels de santé dans la conception et la mise en œuvre d'initiatives de plaidoyer stratégique destinées à améliorer les politiques publiques et l'offre des services de santé. Après quatre ans de mise en œuvre, des progrès ont été observés dans plusieurs domaines prioritaires, tels que la santé maternelle, la vaccination et l'introduction de nouvelles innovations sanitaires. Une rencontre internationale a été ouverte, hier, mercredi 7 octobre, à Dakar, sur le thème : « Les associations des professionnels de santé : des acteurs stratégiques pour le renforcement durable des systèmes de santé en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre ». Le Dr Oumar Sagna, conseiller technique du directeur général de la Santé au ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique, a invité à l’utilisation des compétences pour un renforcement du système de santé. « Cette démarche suppose une réflexion concertée sur les rôles des différentes professions, leur complémentarité et les conditions dans lesquelles elles exercent », a-t-il dit. M. Sagna a rappelé que le partage des tâches doit être accompagné de formations adaptées, de protocoles clairs, d’une supervision effective et de mécanismes de référence fonctionnels. Ce partage doit, à son avis, garantir la sécurité des patients tout en permettant d’élargir l’accès à des prestations de qualité. Oumar Sagna a aussi salué le rôle déterminant des associations professionnelles de santé. « Leur participation est nécessaire pour identifier les évolutions pertinentes, accompagner les équipes et construire des solutions compatibles avec les réalités des services. » À l’en croire, le partenariat entre associations professionnelles, institutions publiques et chercheurs peut renforcer la qualité du plaidoyer. Pour sa part, Maty Dia, directrice exécutive de l’Ong Enda Santé, a déclaré que les bailleurs de fonds se retirent de plus en plus et il y a moins de financement. « L’intérêt du plaidoyer, c’est d’inverser la tendance, afin que ces derniers continuent de nous appuyer, mais aussi que les gouvernements investissent davantage dans la santé », a-t-elle plaidé. Le Dr Papa Djibril Ndoye, directeur adjoint d’Enda Santé, a, lui, précisé que le plaidoyer stratégique s’adresse aux décideurs. « Cette initiative travaille avec six associations de santé dans les trois pays concernés. Il s’agit de médecins, de gynécologues et de nutritionnistes qui mènent ce plaidoyer pour un changement », a-t-il indiqué. Serigne Mansour Sy CISSÉ

items.title: Bokpin cautions Ghana against abandoning existing partnerships over BRICS membership
items.description: Professor of Finance at the University of Ghana Business School and Economist, Professor Godfred Bokpin, has cautioned the government against pursuing Ghana’s proposed membership of BRICS as a strategy to abandon its existing international partnerships or align itself exclusively with a particular political bloc. He said Ghana should approach its BRICS application as part of a broader foreign and economic policy strategy that allows the country to engage with different global economic powers while protecting its interests. Speaking on the Joy FM Super Morning Show on Thursday, October 8, during a discussion on Ghana’s quest to join BRICS, Prof Bokpin said the country needed to be clear about what it wanted to achieve from membership. “Joining BRICS necessarily should not be pursued as a substitution strategy for exiting other blocs or within other political leanings that we have,” he said. He said Ghana should recognise that although BRICS has become an important force in the global economy, the country still has other strategic partners whose interests must be considered. “We need to situate all of this within the broader foreign policy and economic policy that allows us to recognise that yes, BRICS is a dominant force, but there are other players also, and remember that there will also be a pushback from our traditional partners as well. They are equally watching,” he said. Prof Bokpin said the government should have a clear strategy covering the country’s objectives, limitations and the period within which it expected to achieve its goals from BRICS membership. “We need to be quite clear on what we allow, what we will not allow, what is the strategy within what transition period and all of that that we are working at and all of that,” he said. “So we need to engage with our eyes open. We need to make this application to join BRICS with our eyes open.” He cautioned that BRICS membership should not be viewed as a quick solution to Ghana’s economic challenges. “Remember that BRICS wasn’t just designed to transform our economy. The motives are quite clear, just like any other economic bloc that you want to join. It’s the same way,” he said. Prof Bokpin drew comparisons with Ghana’s participation in the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), saying membership of a regional or international economic bloc did not automatically translate into economic benefits. He said Ghana’s ratification of the AfCFTA agreement did not, by itself, guarantee that Ghanaian businesses would become competitive across the continent. “In fact, when we started talking about African Continental Free Trade and all of that, it was quite clear to us that the fact that we are a member, we signed, we submitted our instrument of ratification, necessarily doesn’t mean that automatically we’ll benefit from the African Continental Free Trade,” he said. “There’s a lot that we have to do to make it even worse.” He said Ghana must first create an environment in which local businesses could compete successfully at home before expecting them to compete in international markets. “The fact that we are hosting the secretariat necessarily doesn’t mean we’ll host the gains emanating from the African Continental Free Trade. This is not a host win. You have to work hard. You have to create the enabling environment for your businesses to be able to compete even within Ghana,” he said. “You are talking about competing and winning within Ghana, then you can talk about competing and winning outside Ghana.” Prof Bokpin said one of the biggest challenges was that many Ghanaian businesses were struggling to compete with imported goods in the domestic market. “Even within Ghana, we are not able to compete and win against foreign imports,” he said. He pointed to Ghana’s inflation figures as an indication of the challenges facing local producers. “Look at our inflation dynamics today. Inflation is a domestic issue, okay? Inflation on locally produced is more higher than inflation on imported items,” he said. He said the situation sent the wrong signal to businesses considering whether to invest in local production. “What signal does this send to entrepreneurs?” he asked. “You are much better off actually importing and putting a local logo on it than setting up a production function in Ghana.” Prof Bokpin said that Ghana could not expect its businesses to compete successfully in international markets if they were unable to compete effectively within the domestic economy. “So even within Ghana here, we have not been able to enable our own firms to be able to compete and win in Ghana, let alone to win outside Ghana,” he said. “To win outside Ghana, you first have to win within Ghana. The Chinese are winning outside China because they have won in China.” He said Ghana therefore needed to build a strong domestic productive base before expecting local companies to take advantage of international trade opportunities. “So without creating that kind of backbone for your own firms to compete and win within, you cannot win without. It doesn’t happen that way,” he said. Prof Bokpin acknowledged the government’s efforts to stabilise the economy and said the next phase should focus more strongly on growth and productive investment. “I know that government is putting in a lot of measures and all of that in terms of recalibrating the economic framework,” he said. Prof Bokpin encouraged the Minister of Finance to use the expected fiscal space to tackle Ghana’s development challenges with greater urgency and scale. “And I want to encourage the Minister of Finance that this is the time for Ghana because we’ve created some fiscal space, and I believe that we need to act at scale and on time to be able to respond to the developmental challenges for us to be able to compete and win within and then we can think about winning without and all of that,” he said. “So I believe that there’s a lot that we have to do, and then we also have to explore collaboration with others as well,” Prof Bokpin added. His comments followed Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa’s indication that Ghana intends to submit an application to join BRICS as the government explores ways to diversify its international partnerships, expand economic opportunities and deepen cooperation with countries in the Global South.

items.title: Premier League clubs fear political interference in Man City appeal
items.description: Some Premier League clubs were so “astonished” by comments made by Andy Burnham – appearing to downplay the verdict against Manchester City – that they are now “concerned” about political interference in the appeal process, sources have told BBC Sport. Senior club figures say they were shocked when they heard the prime minister tell the BBC he would be “really concerned” if Manchester City’s owners decide to sell up after the club were found guilty of Premier League financial rule breaches. They have questioned what his comments to the BBC were designed to achieve, and said it had put the Independent Football Regulator in a difficult position. Burnham is under increasing pressure surrounding his relationship with the club’s Abu Dhabi ownership during his time as mayor of Greater Manchester. Such is the level of scrutiny that Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has demanded that No 10 release all details of meetings between the prime minister and senior figures at the club. Despite clarification from Downing Street that Burnham’s view is that no-one is “above the rules”, his comments have sparked unease among some senior Labour figures who fear his initial comments have had major cut-through with voters. Senior club sources have said they found the comments “absolutely bizarre”, and that it was “at best naive and at worst quite manipulative, and that is not a good look”. A different source said it was “clumsy”, while another said they were surprised that the prime minister had “misspoken”. The entire process involving the charges against Manchester City is independent of the Premier League. An independent commission held a 42-day hearing in 2024 which led to the verdict announced last month, with a sanctions hearing still to come. A separate independent appeal board will hear City’s appeal. The club continues to deny any wrongdoing. However, when asked about potential interference in the process off the back of Burnham’s comments, one senior club source said: “Everyone would have a degree of concern. How much would depend on how much you read into that comment. “I think everyone is concerned. Because no-one is stupid around the table. We understand the geopolitics as well. We understand the investment they have made in our country. I don’t think anyone could doubt that or criticise that. But this is different, this is sport, this is our national game.” Another club source, however, said the degree of scrutiny on Burnham now means they think any interference would be impossible. This is a sensitive area for the prime minister. Manchester City ‘s dominance of English football has overlapped in large part both with a period of economic growth for the city of Manchester, and with Burnham’s nine years as mayor from 2017 until earlier this year. As mayor, Burnham championed investment from the Gulf to grow Manchester’s economy, a strategy that had been pursued by the city’s leaders before Burnham became the inaugural elected mayor of the Greater Manchester Combined Authority. Regardless of Burnham’s past career, there are additional sensitivities that would apply to other prime ministers as well. The UK as a whole is eager to trade with the UAE, and the country is an important diplomatic ally in the region at a time of turmoil and war. When the guilty verdicts were announced, Richard Masters, the Premier League’s chief executive, said the club had “systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade”. Burnham’s comments came in an interview with the BBC’s political editor Chris Mason the next day. When asked about ‘Brand Manchester’ taking a hit, the Prime Minister drew a parallel with a previous Premier League case with Everton , saying he still held the view “firmly” that they “weren’t fairly treated”. Everton were deducted 10 points, later reduced to six on appeal , by an independent commission for breaching Premier League financial rules. Asked if he was concerned that Manchester City ‘s owners would now sell the club, Burnham said: “I would be really concerned to lose them. “They’ve been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester and obviously the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is. “I do actually thank the City Football Group and the wider ownership for the money that they didn’t just put into the Etihad [Stadium] and the campus around it but also into the city,” he added. Burnham’s comments provoked strong criticism. The following day, a No 10 spokesperson sought to clarify the comments, saying: “As the prime minister made clear, the initial judgement is serious and there can’t be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules. He also stressed that it is an ongoing independent process. It is essential that it is allowed to run its course and the outcome respected. “If wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences.” However, this statement was amended following further criticism over the use of the word “if” – which was changed to “wherever”. The Premier League is viewed by governments of different political stripes as one of the country’s major cultural exports, so ministers are eager for the row not to cause lasting damage to its brand. Additionally, being a football fan is a core part of Burnham’s political persona. He is an Everton season ticket holder and, prior to becoming prime minister, he spoke of hoping to continue sitting in his usual seat at Hill Dickinson Stadium – but this has not been possible because of security concerns, as was the case for Sir Keir Starmer, his Arsenal -supporting predecessor. Last month Burnham floated the prospect of lifting the ban on football fans drinking in the stands, though it was quickly clarified that this is not in fact government policy.

items.title: VSA and VIA crown 18th anniversary with full scholarships for three brilliant students
items.description: Virtual Security Africa Limited (VSA) and Virtual Infosec Africa Limited (VIA) have awarded full scholarships to three brilliant but needy students to pursue university education at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). The scholarships cover tuition and approved university fees, as well as accommodation and living expenses for the duration of their programmes. The award crowns the Company’s 18th anniversary celebrations, which began with its sponsorship of a complete upgrade of the CCTV surveillance system at Mamprobi Hospital to strengthen the safety of patients, mothers and newborns. For 18 years, VSA and VIA have secured what matters in Ghana’s electronic and cybersecurity space. Today, that commitment extends to the nation’s future leaders. The 2026/27 scholars with their families, management and staff of VSA and VIA, and coordinators from the St. Peter’s SHS Old Boys Association The beneficiaries are; Amankwah Alexander Bempong, Medicine. From Akim Oda, Alexander completed St. Peter’s Senior High School in 2023, achieving 8A1s in his WASSCE, but despite his ambition, he remained at home due to financial hardship. His wait is over: he begins medical studies at KNUST in the 2026/27 academic year. His journey highlights the difference timely support can make in the life of a young person with the ability and ambition to succeed. Reuben Ayitey, Electrical Engineering. From Nsawam, Reuben completed St. Peter’s Senior High School in 2026 with 7A1s and proceeds directly to KNUST in the 2026/27 academic year. Emmanuel Nsowaa Junior, Computer Engineering. From Asempaneye in the Western North Region, Emmanuel completed St. Peter’s Senior High School in 2026 with 7A1s and begins his studies at KNUST in the 2026/27 academic year. Presenting the awards, the Chief Executive Officer, Emmanuel Asiedu, urged the scholars to study diligently, remember their beginnings, and grow into leaders who will one day extend the same support to others. He assured them of the Company’s continued support throughout their journey under the Scheme. The Executive General Manager, Mrs Salomey Armoo, added: “As a company, we protect what matters. Through this Scheme, we are investing in what matters most: people, and the future they will build for a better Ghana.” On behalf of the families, Mrs Comfort Gomado, mother of Reuben Ayitey, expressed profound appreciation to the Chief Executive Officer, the Board, and the Management of VSA and VIA for investing in their children’s future. The initiative reflects VSA and VIA’s commitment to supporting education and contributing to the development of young people and communities. As the three scholars begin their university journey, the Company remains hopeful that this opportunity will not only transform their individual lives but also enable them to make meaningful contributions to Ghana in the years ahead.
