items.title: Pakistan vows to take trade, economic ties with Bahrain to 'new heights'
items.description: Pakistan on Thursday pledged to take trade and economic ties with Bahrain to “new heights” as the two countries held the third session of their Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC) in Islamabad. Bahrain’s FM Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani — who arrived in Pakistan last night on a two-day visit — co-chaired the JMC session along with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar. Addressing a joint press briefing with the Bahrain FM, Dar thanked Al Zayani and his delegation for “their constructive engagement and their very valuable contribution to the success of today’s JMC session”. “Pakistan-Bahrain friendship remains strong and forward-looking, and we are brotherly nations, with long fraternal ties, cooperating on international foras and meeting very frequently wherever we get an opportunity like brothers,” the DPM said. He expressed Pakistan’s commitment to “building an even more prosperous future together, God-willing, and taking the trade and economic ties to a new height”. Dar said Islamabad looked forward to the convening of the JMC’s fourth session in Bahrain in 2027 as both sides will try to hold the meetings every year. “My brother has taken a commitment from me that, unlike today’s session which has been held after five years, I have to find a day for the next one in 365 days during 2027.” Dar also raised the issue of India’s unilateral decision to place the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance, terming it a “material breach of international law”. “Such actions jeopardise the water, food and energy security of Pakistan’s 250 million people,” the deputy premier stressed. Responding to a query, FM Dar said Islamabad and Manama were “connected on all international foras, [and] work and consult with each other”. In his remarks, the Bahraini minister noted that today’s JMC meeting covered “more than 15 fields”. He said both sides agreed to establish a joint working group on trade and investment, as well as to convene the joint working group on energy next month on oil, gas and minerals. They also agreed to take forward cooperation in food security, information technology, law enforcement, media, labour mobility, health, education, culture and sports. “We also committed to finalising the GCC-Pakistan free trade agreement,” he said, referring to the potential deal with the Gulf Cooperation Council that was said to be near finalisation in late 2025. The minister further said that Bahrain, having the GCC presidency, was working to “speed up the signing or the approval of the GCC-Pakistan FTA”. Responding to a query, the visiting dignitary described the bilateral relationship between Pakistan and Bahrain as “very healthy and strong”. He added that it was “radiant and well-looked after” by Bahrain’s King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa and Crown Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa. “It is really valued by the people of Bahrain,” he added. Highlighting recent bilateral exchanges between their countries, FM Al Zayani said: “We have a very truthful relationship; we are so frank with each other. We understand the constraints on each other and work accordingly.” Emphasising the consistency in their ties, with no “ups and downs”, he said, “We are consistent and growing. We feel safe in this relationship.” Al Zayani expressed Manama’s appreciation for Islamabad’s “principled positions on the ongoing crisis”, including its support in March for a United Nations Security Council resolution condemning Iranian attacks on GCC countries. The minister also praised Pakistan’s “efforts alongside other partners to facilitate US-Iran dialogue and de-escalation, including by hosting the Islamabad Talks ” in April. The Bahrain FM went on to strongly condemn the recent deadly “terrorist attacks” on Saudi Arabia’s Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport. He also condemned the “Houthi terrorist militia’s attacks on civilians and civilian facilities in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and its assault” on the holy cities of Makkah and Madina . Noting that targeting of civilian facilities was a “flagrant violation” of international law, Al Zayani affirmed Bahrain’s solidarity with Saudi Arabia “whose security is an integral part of our own and of the GCC”. The Bahrain FM said he and Dar also discussed the crises in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, where “commercial vessels continue to come under attack”. They underscored the importance of freedom and safety of navigation and respect for international law, he added. Al Zayani vowed Bahrain and Pakistan will continue “close coordination” at the UNSC and between their Missions in New York. The visiting FM noted that the two countries will mark 55 years of diplomatic relations on Oct 14. Al Zayani remarked that the “bonds of brotherhood, trust and solidarity […] gained fresh momentum with the official visits to Bahrain” of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in November 2025 and of President Asif Ali Zardari in January this year. The minister noted that more than 140,000 Pakistanis in Bahrain contributed to its progress and “form a living bridge between our peoples”. The Bahrain FM said he would also meet with PM Shehbaz, President Zardari and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir during his visit. JMC meeting During the JMC meeting, Islamabad and Manama “agreed to deepen collaboration in trade and investment, energy, agriculture and food security, information technology, health, education and labour”, FO said. They also discussed measures to strengthen connectivity and promote people-to-people exchanges. Dar “underscored the importance of translating the longstanding and fraternal ties between Pakistan and Bahrain into tangible benefits for their people”. He further stressed effective implementation of the agreed outcomes through joint working groups, institutional partnerships and regular follow-up, FO added. The JMC was attended by high-level delegations from both sides. The Pakistani team included the secretaries of the Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) and the Economic Affairs Division, along with the acting foreign secretary. The Bahraini side included senior officials and representatives of the Bahrain Chamber of Commerce and Industry. In his address to the JMC meeting, Dar reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to increase bilateral trade with Bahrain to the $1 billion target set earlier . Noting the target of doubling trade in three years, of which one has already elapsed, Dar quipped, “But God forbid, if we miss [the target by] a few months, we have a great excuse that this period has been very turbulent.” Dar also referred to a potential free trade agreement (FTA) with the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), noting that the GCC secretary general told him the deal was “almost ripe”, barring one country, which still needed to give a green light. “I’m sure the signing of the free trade agreement between the GCC and Pakistan will surely help us in achieving our goals,” the deputy premier said, adding that it would lead to an increase in imports and exports. “What we need is to complement government-to-government efforts with business-to-business,” the minister stressed. He requested the Bahraini side to work towards recognising degrees and professional qualifications, while facilitating greater mobility of skilled labour between the two countries. Bilateral meeting Prior to the Pakistan-Bahrain JMC, the two foreign ministers also held a separate meeting after Al Zayani’s arrival at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. In a post on X about the “cordial” meeting, the Foreign Office (FO) said the two ministers “reviewed Pakistan–Bahrain relations and expressed satisfaction at the positive momentum in high-level engagement between the two countries”. “They discussed ways to further expand bilateral cooperation across areas of mutual interest, particularly in trade, economic and investment relations, as well as through engagement at multilateral fora.” The two sides also exchanged views on “regional and international developments of mutual interest and underscored that dialogue and diplomacy remain the most viable means of addressing challenges and resolving disputes”, FO added. According to an earlier FO statement, the two sides were to “review the entire spectrum of bilateral relations and discuss ways to further strengthen cooperation across diverse areas of mutual interest, including trade, investment, economic cooperation, defence and security, labour and manpower, and cultural exchanges”. “Pakistan and Bahrain enjoy close, brotherly relations founded on shared faith, common values, mutual respect, and longstanding people-to-people links,” FO noted. Dar and Al Zayani last met in September on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, where they discussed bilateral relations, including preparations for the JMC session. They also exchanged views on regional and international developments, with Al Zayani appreciating Pakistan’s constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability. Pak-Bahrain exchanges Islamabad and Manama had agreed to establish the JMC in 2014, when King Sheikh Hamad bin Isa bin Salman Al-Khalifa paid a three-day visit to Pakistan. Following the last JMC session in July 2021, which was held in Manama, the two countries signed a memorandum of understanding to promote business between the two countries. Earlier this month, Dar chaired an inter-ministerial meeting to review preparations for the Pakistan-Bahrain JMC and directed the ministries concerned to pursue concrete outcomes from the Bahrain FM’s visit. The Pakistani leadership has also undertaken official visits to the Gulf kingdom in recent years. PM Shehbaz, accompanied by Dar, made a two-day trip to Bahrain in November 2025, during which he met with the king and crown prince there. Then, in January this year, President Zardari made a four-day trip to the kingdom, where he highlighted economic opportunities that Pakistan offers.

items.title: Géopolitique, économie et prospective : les entreprises face aux nouveaux désordres mondiaux
items.description: Quatre méga-disruptions structurent l’environnement économique contemporain : géopolitique, climatique, technologique et démographique. Elles s’intensifient, interagissent et produisent des effets en cascade sur l’activité des entreprises. Celles-ci sont conscientes des enjeux vertigineux qui caractérisent notre époque, avec parfois un temps d’avance sur les pouvoirs publics, non seulement en termes d’identification des risques et des ruptures potentielles, mais aussi sur le plan de l’adaptation opérationnelle pour y faire face. En France, elles sont nombreuses ces entreprises, de grande, moyenne ou de petite taille (PME), à comprendre qu’elles évoluent dans un contexte mondial profondément transformé, assurément moins confortable pour les performances européennes. La mondialisation des dernières décennies a souvent été analysée sous l’angle de l’intensification des interdépendances. Celles-ci n’ont pas disparu. Mais leur signification change de registre. Une interdépendance peut simultanément constituer une source d’efficacité économique et une vulnérabilité géopolitique, à plus forte raison si des acteurs s’avèrent déterminés à l’arsenaliser. Nous sommes entrés depuis la pandémie de Covid-19 dans ce que j’ai qualifié de « temps géopolitique des hippopotames » [1] , avec un durcissement des relations internationales et intersociales, une accélération générale dans tous les domaines avec des événements majeurs qui se succèdent rapidement et une multipolarité stratégique où l’on opère en fonction d’intérêts spécifiques, sans aucune attache durable et avec le souci de diversifier au maximum son rapport aux autres. Les hippopotames sont féroces, véloces et polygames, à l’image de cette nouvelle géopolitique mondiale. Convergence des affrontements, réduction des délais de réaction avec montée parallèle de l’impatience, transactionnalisme comme parangon moderne des relations internationales et intersociales. Pour un État, mais surtout pour une entreprise, cela signifie trois choses : défendre ses positions et valoriser ses atouts, préserver une clairvoyance et une autonomie de décision au milieu des tempêtes, maximiser les bénéfices de chaque action ou relation. La montée des risques accroît les tensions. Pour les entreprises, cette évolution impose de dépasser une approche essentiellement défensive du risque. La capacité à détecter les transformations, à explorer plusieurs futurs possibles et à préparer des réponses avant que les ruptures ne se matérialisent devient un facteur de compétitivité. La prospective stratégique n’est plus un exercice de réflexions périphériques. Elle participe de plus en plus de la robustesse de l’organisation d’une entreprise et de sa capacité à survivre dans le monde actuel. D’où l’appel [2] à la multiplication de fonctions inédites sur le versant géopolitique pour que des entreprises puissent s’équiper, en interne, de personnes à même de regarder la planète à 360 degrés et de faire des liens entre des sujets a priori distincts. Beaucoup de jeunes en France se tournent vers des formations en géopolitique. Il devient essentiel d’intégrer la prospective et l’économie dans ces parcours afin de cultiver des champs de vision plus aguerris, et se préparer à des fonctions dans le secteur privé, pour un véritable ancrage dans le réel. La géopolitique quitte en effet les marges de la stratégie d’entreprise, la prospective s’avère de plus en plus nécessaire et l’économie constitue un déterminant majeur des relations internationales et des dynamiques sociales. Vouloir distinguer ces trois domaines serait une erreur. En associant géopolitique, prospective et économie, l’analyse des risques dépasse de loin la gestion. Elle gagne en intelligence stratégique, car répétons-le, le défi pour une entreprise sera d’appréhender l’intensification, la combinaison et la propagation des risques. Pas uniquement leur existence avérée ou probable. Pour les entreprises, la gestion des risques restera bien entendu indispensable. Identifier les vulnérabilités, évaluer leur probabilité, mesurer leurs conséquences et organiser des réponses constituent les fondements de toute stratégie de résilience. Mais cette démarche repose principalement et généralement sur des risques identifiés. Or l’une des caractéristiques de la période contemporaine réside précisément dans l’importance croissante des ruptures difficiles à probabiliser et dans les interactions entre différentes catégories de risques. Un événement climatique ou géopolitique peut interrompre une fluidité logistique, provoquer une rupture d’approvisionnement, affecter une production industrielle, créer de l’inflation et générer ensuite des tensions économiques ou sociales. Il faut donc compléter la gestion des risques par une intelligence des risques : observer l’environnement global en s’efforçant de comprendre pourquoi tout le monde ne pense pas et n’agit pas comme nous le faisons, identifier les interdépendances critiques, suivre les signaux faibles sans omettre de concentrer son attention sur des transformations structurelles silencieuses, croiser les disciplines et surveiller les dynamiques qui se situent hors du champ traditionnel de l’entreprise. En somme, sortir de son couloir de nage, accepter des températures variables de l’eau et avoir conscience de l’ondulation incessante des vagues. La vie d’une entreprise n’est pas un long fleuve tranquille, tout comme sa performance n’est jamais un acquis garanti. C’est aussi pour cette raison que l’on recrutera des tempéraments avant de regarder des talents. Dans un monde plus nerveux et moins stable, avec des entreprises aux activités sans cesse en mouvement, l’état d’esprit et les comportements comptent. Ils peuvent même faire la différence, lors de recrutements, mais surtout d’évolutions de postes et de rôles dans l’entreprise. C’est ici qu’il convient d’insister sur ce que l’on entend par prospective stratégique. Elle ne consiste pas à prédire l’avenir ! Elle part au contraire du principe que plusieurs futurs sont possibles et cherche à préparer l’entreprise à différents environnements, parfois très contrastés [3] . Dit autrement, la finalité de la prospective n’est donc pas d’avoir raison sur le futur et ce qu’il adviendra pour sûr. Sa fonction est de réduire l’effet de surprise stratégique pour une entreprise. Nuance de taille, car il s’agit bien ici de s’assurer de moyens techniques et humains capables d’encaisser un choc éventuel, de réagir sans être tétanisés, de le faire en ordre groupé et avec une planification pragmatique, afin non seulement de favoriser la continuité opérationnelle des activités (ou du moins d’en éviter la rupture fatale), mais aussi d’entrevoir des opportunités dans chaque moment décisif. D’ailleurs, il peut s’avérer parfois pertinent d’être audacieux et très entreprenant dans les séquences pourtant les plus sensibles. En Europe et en France, il est temps de tirer le rideau sur un monde définitivement lointain, où de manière illusoire et arrogante, nous avons été sensibles aux sirènes de la fin de l’Histoire, de l’effacement de la géographie et de l’inutilité de l’économie. Le réveil peut être brutal pour certains. Nous devons nous interroger sur notre place dans le monde, nos atouts cultivables et nos fragilités incontournables. Nous devons réfléchir à la trajectoire de nos démocraties, qui n’ont plus fait ces dernières décennies, l’expérience d’un rétropédalage des conditions de sécurité ou des niveaux de vie. Nous devons aller plus loin dans les transitions écologiques sans pour autant nous désarmer sur le plan productif et économique. Les transformations mondiales, qu’elles soient géopolitiques, climatiques, technologiques ou démographiques, amènent les sociétés européennes à des arbitrages plus nombreux. Il est même urgent de savoir prioriser, faute de capacités d’investissement illimité, pour ne pas dire qu’elles sont d’ores et déjà amoindries. Cette période stratégique moins confortable n’est pas nécessairement déclinante. Nous sommes plutôt devant une exigence collective de nouveaux efforts à faire. Sortons du fatalisme avec l’idée d’une Europe ou d’une France qui tel le Titanic sombrerait assurément. Évitons le toboggan expliquant que la chute constitue l’unique chemin possible. Acceptons en revanche le trail que nous avons à réaliser, comportant des obstacles, des dénivelés, des changements de rythme et des difficultés imprévues. Un trail qui implique de bons équipements pour aller de l’avant, une mentalité mixant discernements et volontés, mais également de l’endurance, de la solidarité et de l’espérance. Il ne s’agit donc pas de rechercher pour un État ou pour une entreprise une improbable maîtrise de l’avenir. La prospective stratégique propose de développer la capacité à opérer dans plusieurs futurs possibles. La complexité de l’époque actuelle ne doit pas conduire à la résignation générale. Nous pouvons trouver la situation déprimante ; elle est surtout exigeante. Il faut donc opposer à la résignation une forme d’ardeur joyeuse : non pas un optimisme ignorant les contraintes et les difficultés, mais une disposition collective à regarder les adversités avec lucidité tout en préservant la capacité d’agir. Dans une démocratie comme dans une entreprise, l’objectif doit être de faire demain mieux qu’hier. Le déclin n’est pas permis, le statu quo est mortifère. Le futur n’est pas une peur, c’est une aventure. [1] Sébastien Abis, « Nourrir le futur à l’ombre des hippopotames », dans Nourrir 2050 : de la fiction à la réalité, Le Déméter 2025 (Paris : Club demeter, IRIS Éditions) : 22-35. [2] Florent Parmentier, Cyrille Bret et Laurent Celerier, Chief Geopolitical Officer . Agir en entrepreneur, penser en géopoliticien (Versailles :Valeurs ajoutées Editions, 2026) [3] Se reporter aux méthodologies et aux travaux de l’association Futuribles international, qui fait référence en la matière, en France comme en Europe. L’article Géopolitique, économie et prospective : les entreprises face aux nouveaux désordres mondiaux est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: The growing protests against India's poll body — and PM Modi
items.description: India’s election commission is facing mounting pressure after a newspaper investigation alleged misconduct during a nationwide voter-roll revision. The Indian Express alleged last month that key decisions linked to the large-scale revision exercise — which has seen millions of names removed from draft voter rolls — were likely taken without the approval of two of the three election commissioners. The Election Commission of India (ECI), a constitutional body, has rejected the allegations. It says all its decisions were unanimous and legally valid. Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) supporters chant slogans, hold placards and wave national flag as they celebrate the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) examination paper leaks, following a protest, in Mumbai, India on July 26, 2026. —Reuters/File Opposition parties say legitimate voters are being struck off to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling party. Protests demanding that commission chief Gyanesh Kumar step down have grown since the report, with a demonstration in the capital New Delhi on Saturday expected to draw large crowds. The allegations are a fresh challenge for 76-year-old Modi, in his third term in office, following student protests in July that forced the education minister to resign. Police detain a demonstrator during a protest demanding the resignation of India’s Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India on October 3, 2026. — Reuters Here is a rundown of the major issues at stake in the latest protest: What’s the controversy? The Indian Express reported that the poll body has been riven by internal disagreements since the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the voter lists began in 2025. It said two of the ECI’s three commissioners formally lodged objections more than a dozen times in the last 10 months over key SIR decisions. Decisions by the three-member poll body should be taken by consensus or a majority. Why has it sparked anger? The poll body says the exercise identifies fraudulently registered voters and aims to prevent “foreign illegal immigrants” from casting ballots. Critics say the drive has disproportionately affected marginalised and minority communities. Members of Modi’s Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India’s electoral rolls. How many are excluded? According to election commission data cited by Indian media, more than 133 million names have been excluded from draft rolls. That’s roughly the population of Mexico and, in the world’s most populous nation, adds up to about 15 per cent of the electorate. Supporters of India’s main opposition Congress party try to remove a police barricade during a protest demanding the resignation of India’s Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India on September 25, 2026. — Reuters The exclusions include duplicate entries and people found to have died. The final count of excluded voters, however, will only be clear after claims and objections are processed and final rolls are published. How big are the protests? Thousands have taken to the streets in protest, and the youth-led online Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) movement launched fresh demonstrations on October 2 in Mumbai. The opposition Congress Party has rallied in New Delhi, with key leader Rahul Gandhi briefly detained on both Tuesday and Wednesday. The CJP, which has millions of followers on social media, succeeded in its campaign to oust the education minister in July over irregularities in exam systems. The movement has called for another “mass mobilisation” on Saturday, supported by student groups aligned with left-wing parties. “Last time when we got together, it was a cabinet minister who had to resign,” said Neha Bora, a student leader who has emerged as one of the faces of the latest protests. “This time, we will see the CEC (chief election commissioner) being ousted.” Who is Kumar? Kumar, 62, is a retired civil servant from the elite Indian Administrative Service. He took charge as election commission chief in February last year and is due to remain in office until January 2029. supporter dressed as an electronic voting machine (EVM) holds a placard during a protest demanding the resignation of India’s Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar organised by the Shiv Sena (UBT) and the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) in Mumbai, India, October 4, 2026. —Reuters Kumar’s civil services journey began in the southern state of Kerala, whose government launched a probe this month into corruption allegations involving him dating back to 2006. What do the courts say? The Supreme Court has ordered the government and election body to explain decisions linked to the voter-roll revision. The legality of the revision exercise has also been examined by the court. In May, it allowed the election commission to proceed with the nationwide exercise, while calling for safeguards to protect eligible voters. Another hearing is due next week.

items.title: Road crashes in Ghana fall 9.48% in September 2026, fatalities drop 7.82% – MTTD
items.description: Road crashes in the country decreased by 9.48% in September 2026, while fatalities fell by 7.82%, according to the Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD). The department’s Director of Education, Research and Training, ACP Alexander Kwaku Obeng, attributed the improvements to increased enforcement against speeding and public education by the Ghana Police Service. He said police data also showed a 12.19% decline in the number of vehicles involved in crashes. Motorcycle crashes decreased by 7.14%, while injuries fell by 15%. ACP Obeng explained that the Police intensified the issuance of electronic violation notices and caution notices from September 10, ahead of the planned nationwide introduction of the automated enforcement system on November 1, 2026. He said speeding remained the initial priority, with sensors being used to detect offences. Drivers and vehicle owners receive electronic notices supported by video evidence showing the violations. According to him, involving vehicle owners in the process had encouraged them to promote responsible driving, while motorists were becoming more cautious. “We issue the ticket to you, and you are confronted with the video; watch it and see what the driver is doing. The owners become advocates and drivers become cautious, and that’s what we have seen,” he said. ACP Obeng said the combination of monitoring, warnings and sensitisation was influencing motorists to reduce their speed. He spoke on Citi FM. “People are beginning to reduce their speeds because we are there, we are sensitising, and we are warning, and we are determined that 1st November will go live,” he added. The Police intend to maintain their focus on speeding as preparations continue for the nationwide rollout.

items.title: Pétition | Pour la libération de Néjib Chebbi et des détenus politiques en Tunisie
items.description: Ahmed Néjib Chebbi a suspendu mercredi 7 octobre 2026 sa grève de la faim . S elon son fils Louay , l’ administration pénitentiaire, qui dit prendre ses revendications au sérieux, s ’ est engagée à garantir aux détenus l ’ accès à une source d ’ information fiable. Après concertation avec sa famille, l’activiste politique a décidé d ’ une suspension temporaire, «en signe de bonne foi», en attendant de vérifier que ces engagements soient tenus. Face à la gravité de la situation, plus de cent cinquante personnalités de France, d ’ Europe, du Maghreb, du monde arabe, d ’ Afrique subsaharienne et du Canada ont signé la pétition reproduite ci-dessous réclamant sa libération, celle de tous les détenu.e.s politiques et d ’ opinion, et le rétablissement des droits et libertés politiques en Tunisie. À 82 ans, Ahmed Néjib Chebbi entame un de ses ultimes combats, mettant une fois encore sa vie en péril. Voilà bientôt soixante ans que cet homme symbolise la résistance contre l’oppression. Du temps de Bourguiba, il faisait partie des étudiants révoltés de mars 1968 emprisonnés pour «complot contre la sûreté de l’État» . Le complot, hier comme aujourd’hui, c’est la traduction de la revendication démocratique en langage despotique. Du temps de Ben Ali, il sera l’une des principales figures de la grande grève de la faim du 18 octobre 2005 pour les libertés, aux côtés de l’avocat Ayachi Hammami, son compagnon d’infortune aujourd’hui, et d’autres militants, de diverses sensibilités politiques. Cible de la vindicte du régime issu du coup de force du 25 juillet 2021, le voilà de nouveau en prison, comme tant d’autres, pour les mêmes raisons : le rêve et le combat pacifique pour les libertés. Et le voilà de nouveau en grève de la faim pour la liberté. Le nom d’Ahmed Néjib Chebbi, doyen des démocrates de ce pays, est devenu l’emblème de la longue résistance contre tous les autoritarismes depuis l’indépendance. Le recours à la grève de la faim pour dénoncer les conditions de détention est un épisode de plus de cette résistance. Dans la Tunisie d’aujourd’hui, tout se passe comme si la persécution permanente des opposant.e.s, en liberté provisoire ou entre quatre murs, est devenue le mode d’existence d’un règne de plus en plus ubuesque. Le recours récurrent à la grève de la faim, de la part des détenu.e.s politiques mettant les uns après les autres leurs vies en péril, apparaît comme l’ultime force des démunis. Face à un régime qui travaille à effacer l’idée même de politique, cette arme ultime est l’affirmation de la pérennité de la lutte pour l’État de droit, la démocratie et les libertés. Nous, signataires, appelons à la libération de Ahmed Néjib Chebbi et des détenu.e.s politiques et d’opinion, ainsi qu’au rétablissement des droits et libertés politiques en Tunisie. items.title: N18m fraud: Man allegedly impersonating Ogun prophet on Facebook arrested
items.description: The Police Command in Ogun has arrested a suspect, Adewale Arojah, for allegedly impersonating a cleric on Facebook and defrauding victims of over N18 million. The command’s Spokesman DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, disclosed this in a statement issued on Thursday in Abeokuta. Babaseyi said the suspect was arrested by operatives of the Ilaro Division following a complaint lodged on Oct. 3 by one Muyiwa Akogun, popularly known on Facebook as “Prophet Dr. Muyiwa Akogun.” He said Akogun had reported that members of the public were complaining about fraudulent activities being carried out through a duplicated Facebook account bearing his identity. According to Babaseyi, the suspect was a spiritual son of Akogun and has allegedly used the cleric’s identity to deceive unsuspecting members of the public. He said upon receipt of the complaint, the Divisional Police Officer (DPO), Ilaro, immediately deployed intelligence and detective operatives to track the suspect. He noted that sustained technological monitoring and intelligence-led investigation led to the suspect’s arrest in a village in Ajegunle, along the Ilaro/Ibogun axis. “Upon his arrest, the suspect confessed during interrogation to impersonating Akogun and using his identity to offer fake prophecies and prayer services to unsuspecting victims. “Preliminary investigation revealed that the suspect targeted people seeking spiritual assistance through the cleric’s Facebook page and allegedly defrauded victims in Nigeria and abroad of over N18 million. “The suspect has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Eleweran, Abeokuta, for further investigation to determine the extent of the alleged offences and identify possible accomplices,” he said. Babaseyi quoted the Commissioner of Police, CP Bode Ojajuni, as commending the Ilaro operatives for their vigilance and swift response. Ojajuni reaffirmed the command’s commitment to tackling cybercrime, identity theft and other forms of criminality in the state. He also advised members of the public to verify the authenticity of social media accounts belonging to religious leaders and public figures before engaging with them. He urged citizens to avoid transferring money to unverified persons for spiritual remedies or other services. The CP encouraged members of the public to report cybercrime, impersonation and suspicious activities through the Gateway Shield toll-free line, 0800 000 9111, or 09164859299 and 09154293464. (NAN) The post N18m fraud: Man allegedly impersonating Ogun prophet on Facebook arrested appeared first on Vanguard News .

Mr Opare Addo made the remarks after receiving members of the Committee at the Ministry of Youth Development and Empowerment on Wednesday, October 7, 2026. The meeting focused on the Ministry’s programmes, achievements and priorities for youth development. The Minister thanked the Committee for its engagement and continued interest in youth development, stressing the importance of sustained collaboration among state institutions. He said such collaboration would help ensure that policies and programmes respond effectively to the needs and aspirations of Ghana’s young people.

items.title: Hausse des prix du gasoil : À Rabat, les chauffeurs de grands taxis menacent de faire grève
items.description: La hausse des tarifs des grands taxis à Rabat n’est pas encore actée. Réunis mercredi pour examiner l’éventualité d’une augmentation d’un dirham sur certaines lignes desservant les quartiers de la capitale, les professionnels du secteur n’ont pas tranché. Selon une source proche des discussions, l’option d’un mouvement de grève reste néanmoins sérieusement envisagée. Cette réunion intervient dans un contexte de forte tension provoqué par l’envolée des prix du gasoil, dont le litre dépasse désormais les 16 dirhams dans les stations-service marocaines. Une situation qui pèse lourdement sur l’activité des chauffeurs, principaux concernés par l’augmentation des coûts d’exploitation. À ce stade, aucune hausse effective des tarifs n’a toutefois été appliquée. Au-delà de la question des carburants, les professionnels dénoncent également des irrégularités dans le versement de la dernière tranche de l’aide publique au carburant, correspondant au mois d’août. « Un climat de mécontentement et de confusion règne parmi les chauffeurs », affirme la même source. Selon les informations recueillies, certaines banques ont versé une aide de 1.100 dirhams à une partie des bénéficiaires lors de la première journée de distribution, avant d’interrompre les opérations en invoquant un manque de liquidités. D’autres chauffeurs n’auraient ainsi perçu que 600 dirhams, alimentant un sentiment d’injustice et de traitement inégal au sein de la profession. Face à cette situation, deux scénarios sont actuellement débattus. Le premier consiste à exiger une harmonisation des modalités de versement de l’aide afin que tous les chauffeurs bénéficient des mêmes montants. Le second prévoit l’abandon de ce mécanisme de soutien en échange d’une augmentation officielle et réglementaire des tarifs, validée par les autorités compétentes. Les représentants du secteur démentent toutefois les informations faisant état d’augmentations déjà appliquées sur certaines lignes, notamment entre Hay Ryad et le centre-ville. La question demeure en discussion et devrait être réexaminée lors d’une nouvelle réunion prévue avant la fin de la semaine, en présence des différentes représentations syndicales. Parallèlement, les professionnels ont adressé un courrier au chef de la division des affaires économiques de la préfecture afin d’engager des concertations avec le wali et le secrétaire général autour des revendications du secteur. Une réunion élargie regroupant les chauffeurs de Rabat, Salé et Témara est également en préparation. L’objectif affiché est de constituer un front commun capable de porter les doléances de la profession auprès des autorités. Ces discussions font suite aux déclarations d’un responsable d’une station de grands taxis de Rabat affiliée à l’Union générale des travailleurs du Maroc (UGTM), qui indiquait mardi à Hespress qu’une hausse d’un dirham était à l’étude sur les lignes reliant Bab Chellah aux quartiers Taqaddoum, Nahda et Youssoufia. La mesure pourrait, selon lui, être étendue aux dessertes vers Salé et Témara. Le même responsable souligne que les dépenses en carburant absorbent désormais la majeure partie des recettes quotidiennes, au point que certains chauffeurs ne dégageraient plus qu’un revenu net de 40 dirhams par jour. De leur côté, les associations de défense des consommateurs rappellent qu’aucune augmentation des tarifs des taxis ne peut entrer en vigueur sans l’adoption préalable d’un arrêté du gouverneur, seule base légale autorisant une révision des prix du transport. The post Hausse des prix du gasoil : À Rabat, les chauffeurs de grands taxis menacent de faire grève appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: 2027: Your PVC is not for sale — Obi Media Office to Nigerians
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA- AHEAD of next year’s elections, the media office of the Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi has urged Nigerians to remain remain vigilant against anyone offering money or inducements in exchange for their votes, advising the people not to sell their Permanent Voters Cards, PVC or participation in any scheme aimed at compromising the electoral process. According to the Peter Obi Media Office, POMR, it said it has become aware of the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC’s strategy of exploiting the poverty in the land—poverty they have created by offering large sums of money to people in exchange for their PVCs. The POMR said to Nigerians that their PVC is not for sale, vote is not for sale, their future is not for sale, just as it urged them to collect their PVC, keep it secure and do not hand it over to anyone, pleading with the people to reject bribes and report any suspected electoral manipulation to the proper authorities, adding that on election day, they should turn out, vote according to their conscience, protect theirbballot, and insist that their votes count. A statement signed on Thursday by the Spokesman of POMR, Idris Zekeri on Thursday read, “Exactly 100 days left to election day, we urge Nigerians to remain vigilant against anyone offering money or inducements in exchange for your vote, your PVC, or participation in any scheme aimed at compromising the electoral process. “Reports from some states indicate that some state governors, who have nothing positive to show to persuade their citizens, including civil servants, are collecting their PVCs in exchange for the payment of their legitimate salaries and allowances. “Your PVC is not for sale. Your vote is not for sale. Your future is not for sale. Collect your PVC. Keep it secure. Do not hand it over to anyone. Reject bribes and report any suspected electoral manipulation to the proper authorities. “On election day, turn out, vote according to your conscience, protect your ballot, and insist that your vote counts. “Hold your PVC firmly. Use it responsibly. Defend your vote legally. Defend your democracy and create a new Nigeria that will be possible and OK.” The post 2027: Your PVC is not for sale — Obi Media Office to Nigerians appeared first on Vanguard News .

2027: Obidient movement still with me – Rhodes-Vivour
items.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate in Lagos State, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, has said the Obidient movement remains with him despite contesting the 2027 governorship election on a different political platform from Peter Obi. Rhodes-Vivour stated this during an interview on BlackBox , a talk show hosted by Rufai Oseni. Asked whether the Peter Obi wave would still work for him in the coming election now that he and the former Anambra State governor are no longer on the same political platform, Rhodes-Vivour said the values that attracted members of the movement to him remained part of his political identity. “I feel that the qualities that movement adopted or welcomed, those are qualities that I still carry. Those are qualities that have been consistent with. I’ve been with them in the trenches,” he said. Rhodes-Vivour said his relationship with members of the movement had continued beyond the 2023 election, adding that he had maintained personal relationships with them and remained involved in their affairs. “Even after the election, the aftermath of the election, hospital bills that were paid, and all of that. We build personal relationships across board,” he said. According to him, his consistency and continued identification with the values of the movement would make him a trusted figure among its members despite the political differences between him and Obi. “I feel that as far as I carry those qualities and those characteristics are still with me, and I’ve shown consistency, I believe that I’m a trusted figure,” Rhodes-Vivour said. “I believe that when push comes to shove, that movement is still with me. That’s just the honest truth.” In the 2023 election, Rhodes-Vivour contested the Lagos governorship election on the platform of the Labour Party while Obi ran for president on the same platform. Obi won Lagos in the presidential election, while Rhodes-Vivour came second in the governorship poll behind incumbent Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu. Ahead of the 2027 election, however, Obi has moved from the Labour Party to the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), where Funso Doherty is the party’s governorship candidate in Lagos. Rhodes-Vivour is seeking the Lagos governorship ticket under the ADC, whose presidential candidate is former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. He recently said he had no issues with Obi, adding that Atiku remained his presidential candidate for the 2027 election. The post 2027: Obidient movement still with me – Rhodes-Vivour appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Court grants alleged fake JAMB registrar N50m bail
items.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja has admitted Mr Arinze Nwogba to a N50 million bail with two sureties in like sum. Justice Salim Ibrahim, in a ruling on Thursday , held that the offence Nwogba allegedly committed was a bailable one, which is not a capital offence for which the punishment is death. “From the affidavit of the defendant/applicant, he has alluded to the fact that he will not jump bail and he will present himself for trial which is the hallmark in bail application.” The judge, who said granting bail is discretionary power of the court, admitted him to N50 million bail with two sureties. He ordered that one of the sureties must be a civil servant, not less than Grade Level 14 in the federal civil service. According to Justice Ibrahim, each of the sureties must be resident within the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, with one of the sureties residing either at Asokoro, Maitama, or Guzape. The judge ordered that each of the sureties must depose to affidavit of means. He ruled that each of the sureties shall submit his or her tax clearance certificate for the past two years. The judge directed the defendant and the sureties to submit their photocopies of their national identification slips. He also directed the registrar of the court to verify the bail documents and issue a report and sign, as well as the prosecution. Justice Ibrahim, therefore, ordered Nwogba to remain in Kuje Correctional Centre pending the perfection of the bail terms. He adjourned the matter until Oct. 19 for commencement of his trial. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the Inspector-General (I-G) of Police is prosecuting Nwogba for allegedly impersonating to be Prof. Segun Aina, Registrar, Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB). The I-G, in the six-count charge marked: FHC/ABJ/CR/612/2026, sued Nwogba as sole defendant The defendant, who was arraigned on Friday by the police, was remanded in Kuje Correctional Centre pending the hearing of his bail application filed by his lawyer. In one of the counts, Nwogba, who resides at No. 16,Emeka Egbe by Roban Stores, Abakaliki in Ebonyi, and others now at large, were alleged to have fraudulently impersonated the JAMB Registrar, Prof. Aina. The defendant was alleged to have registered his picture on whatsapp profile and true caller on telephone number: 08139433155 with the intent to gain financial advantage to himself. The offence is said to be contrary to and punishable under Section 22(3)(a)(b) & (4) of the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, Etc) Act, 2015 Amended 2024. The prosecution, in the brief fact of the case, said a petition was written and submitted to the I-G by the board registrar concerning the activities of some suspected criminal gangs who fraudulently registered and are using the telephone number and pictures of Prof. Aina without his knowledge and authority. The police alleged that these individuals were using the identity of the JAMB registrar to deceive unsuspecting members of the public. It said they equally went on LinkedIn and published the said number where they directed unsuspecting innocent citizens to contact them only through WhatsApp using the number. “The investigating team decided to engage the fraudsters directly using the WhatsApp number he advertised on LinkedIn. “The fraudsters who already used the image of JAMB registrar as profile pictures both on WhatsApp and truecaller in order to deceive innocent Nigerians informed his victims that he wants to offer them a contract and he has obtained necessary approvals from the Minister of Education.” According to the document, in his text message on WhatsApp, he stated, “Federal Ministry of Education Abuja has approved the supply of 200 units of HP laptops to us as a part of our digitization programs.” It alleged that the acclaimed JAMB registrar also sent the contact of his personal assistant as (07017626031) who he described as Dr Stephen Igwe and who would be representing him to make all the arrangement for the award of the contract. “He equally directed that his PA will send an account number where he directed the sum of N900,000 to be paid for handshake. “He equally ordered the payment of another three (3) million naira into the account for the permanent secretary and Minister of Education. “He equally sent an access bank account number 1572799985 with account name: EDEH CHIMEZIE BENEDICT. “He requested for an initial deposit of nine hundred thousand naira (N900,000) to be used to bribe the members of staff at the minister’s office,” the prosecution alleged, among others. It said Nwogba whose operational name was Dr. Stephen Igwe was subsequently arrested in Abakallki in Ebonyi. “He confessed that the account details belong to his late nephew who died in April 2026 and was buried on July 31. “He admitted that he actually forwarded the details of the account to his cousin, one NNABUIFE NWEKPA ‘M’ of Onitsha, Anambra State to use for the fraudulent activity. “The said NNABUIFE NWEKPA (the acclaimed fake JAMB Registrar) is now on the run and currently at large. “Serious efforts are being intensified to arrest the fleeing suspect,” the police told the court. (NAN) The post Court grants alleged fake JAMB registrar N50m bail appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: BRICS membership won’t transform Ghana’s economy without domestic reforms – Bokpin
items.description: Professor of Finance at the University of Ghana Business School and Economist, Professor Godfred Bokpin, has cautioned that Ghana’s decision to join the BRICS economic bloc should not be seen as a substitute for the domestic reforms needed to transform the country’s economy. He said that while joining BRICS could provide Ghana with new economic opportunities and strengthen its engagement with emerging global economies, membership alone would not automatically improve the country’s economic fortunes. Speaking on the Joy FM Super Morning Show on Thursday, October 8, during a discussion on Ghana’s quest to join BRICS, Prof Bokpin said the country must continue to focus on managing its economy competitively regardless of its international affiliations. “I think we should just bear in mind that BRICS is still evolving, even within the original founding members, in terms of the framework, where exactly this is heading towards, and all of that. And so there are quite a lot of nuances that would have to be ironed out of that,” he said. He said that Ghana should not expect BRICS membership to deliver an immediate economic transformation. “But it is good to also say that merely joining BRICS necessarily does not transform your economy overnight, or even over a 15-year period,” Prof Bokpin said. “It is not a substitute for what you have to do in managing your own economy competitively, and all of that.” Despite the caution, Prof Bokpin said he supported the government’s intention to join the bloc, arguing that the global economic balance was shifting and Ghana needed to position itself accordingly. “If I look at it from an economic perspective, it’s a good move that the government plans to join BRICS. That is where the world is heading towards, and that is a fact,” he said. He pointed to the growing economic influence of BRICS, saying the combined economic output of its member countries had become significant enough to rival or exceed that of traditional Western-led economic groupings. “If you look at the commanding position of BRICS within the global economy today, the combined GDP of BRICS, especially across the 11 founding members, and then also the 10 partner countries today, actually exceeds the GDP of the G7 that we used to know,” he said. According to Prof Bokpin, the bloc now accounts for a substantial share of the global economy and its members have strong growth prospects. “It accounts for almost 40 percent of the global GDP. The BRICS member countries have higher growth potential today than literally any other economic bloc you can think about,” he said. Prof Bokpin said long-term economic projections also pointed to a growing role for BRICS countries in the global economy. He noted that China was projected to remain the world’s largest economy by 2050, while the United States was expected to rank second. “It may interest you to know that by 2050, three out of the top five big economies globally will all be BRICS members,” he said. “Three out of the top five by 2050.” He said the projected shift in the global economic order also helped explain some of the growing tensions between the United States and China. “In fact, by 2050, China will be number one, and the U.S. will be number two in terms of the global economic order,” Prof Bokpin said. “You can understand this also gives you a perspective as to the tension between the U.S. and China and all of that. It’s all playing out carefully within the global geopolitics, and how the global order, some want it to be rewritten in a certain way, and all of that.” Looking further ahead, Prof Bokpin said economic projections for 2075 showed an even stronger presence of BRICS countries among the world’s largest economies. He said four of the five largest economies by then were projected to be BRICS members. “And that said, it’s also important to look at the world economic projections. By 2075, the top five economies in the world measured in USD, actually there will only be one that will not be a BRICS member,” he said. “So four out of the top five big economies by 2075, four of them will be BRICS members.” He also highlighted Nigeria’s projected position among the world’s largest economies, saying the country’s growth could be driven by its private sector and major entrepreneurs. “In fact, the projection is that by 2075, Nigeria will be in the top five. And this may surprise a lot of people,” he said. Prof Bokpin, however, cautioned against treating such projections as certainties. “I’m not asking people to put on faith to believe in this,” he said, explaining that the projection was based partly on the potential of Nigeria’s large entrepreneurs and the transformation of its private sector. He said that the country’s economic transformation would not depend solely on government but could also be driven by major Nigerian entrepreneurs. “The understanding is that if you look at what Nigeria is doing, the transformation is going to come from big Nigerian entrepreneurs, billionaires, who have decided, and it’s not just Aliko Dangote,” he said. Prof Bokpin said Ghana was already experiencing the growing influence of emerging economies through its expanding economic relationship with China, even without being a member of BRICS. He said Ghana needed to recognise the changing patterns of global trade and position itself accordingly. “So if you put all of that together, and we have no joint business, actually, but today, China has literally taken over our markets, whether you like it or not, right?” he said. “So the traffic today is within the Ghana-China corridor as compared to our traditional import-oriented countries and all of that. So we need to just look at all of that.” He said these developments provided an economic basis for Ghana to consider closer engagement with BRICS, although other considerations would also have to be examined. “So in terms of where the world is moving towards and all of that, it will look to me that it’s a good decision. Of course, I’m looking at it purely from an economics perspective,” Prof Bokpin said. “There may be geopolitical, there may be other considerations that would also have to come to the table and all of that.” Prof Bokpin, however, cautioned that Ghana should not expect BRICS membership to resolve its economic challenges. “So specifically for Ghana, I think that merely joining BRICS would not necessarily transform our economy,” he said.

items.title: Government spends GH¢917m on No-Fees-Stress policy for 321,807 students
items.description: The government has so far spent GH¢917 million to support students under the No-Fees-Stress Policy, the Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, has revealed. He said the money, which covered 321,807 students, was paid from budgetary support from the Consolidated Fund. The GH¢917 million is a direct flow from the Ministry of Finance from the Consolidated Fund as part of the Ministry of Education’s budgetary support. Other releases have gone to the Students Loan Trust Fund (SLTF) from the Ghana Education Trust Fund (GETFund) for the students loan disbursement,” he said. Mr Iddrisu said this yesterday at a Stakeholder Engagement on the Implementation of the No-Fees-Stress Initiative at Dawu in the Eastern Region. The programme, organised by the SLTF, is on the theme: “Strengthening No-Fees-Stress Implementation through Institutional Partnerships for Inclusive, Equitable and Sustainable Student Financing”. It is being attended by representatives of Vice-Chancellors Ghana, Vice-Chancellors of Technical Universities, Principals of Colleges of Education, Federation of Ghana Medical Students, civil society organisations (CSOs) and the Parliamentary Select Committee on Education. Mr Iddrisu said in the 2024 National Democratic Congress Resetting Ghana Manifesto, President John Mahama committed to reducing the financial burden of tertiary education students and their families. In pursuit of that, he said on July 4, 2025, that commitment was translated into action with the launch of the No-Fees-Stress Initiative, implemented by the SLTF and adequately funded by the GetFund. “Let me commend the management and leadership of the Students Loan Trust Fund, and the leadership and management of GetFund, for keeping this dream a reality under President Mahama’s Reset. “Arguably, and statistically, GH¢917 million has so far been spent to support students under the No-Fee-Stress, covering a student population of 321,807 students,” he emphasised. He admitted that one of the major challenges of the No-Fee-Stress Policy had to do with timely releases of budgetary allocation for its implementation. He, therefore, stressed the need to ensure the timely release of funds in order not to defeat the purpose of the initiative. “So regardless of your financial standing, regardless of your geographical location, regardless of the status of your parents, an eligible Ghanaian who qualifies to access higher education must be supported by government to access higher education,” he said. He indicated that the No-Fees-Stress Policy had come to stay. Mr Iddrisu said the government had opened up the student loan trust support to students studying Law for the first time in many years and demystified legal education. “We will do the same for medical education in the coming years. As a true value of human capital development, maybe we should now accept that human capital development be construed as a strategic investment requirement of every government and sufficient budgetary allocation provided for it,” he said. Presenting an update on the No-Fees-Stress Policy, the Chief Executive Officer of the SLTF, Dr Saajida Shiraz, said the fund was a statutory agency under the Ministry of Education with a mandate to provide financial resources for the benefit of tertiary students and in the last one-and-a-half years, “we are contending with what we describe as an expanded mandate to the introduction of the government’s flagship No-Fees-Stress Policy, which is a transformational initiative by President John Dramani Mahama to ensure that financial circumstance would not become a barrier to accessing tertiary education for any Ghanaian student”. The No-Fees-Stress Policy, she said, had five sub-components — no academic fee policy, the free tertiary education for persons with disabilities, students loan plus initiative, enhanced traditional loan scheme with higher loan amounts and reduced interest rates, and digitalisation of the system to make it easier to access loans. “So for this academic year, we came up with a very creative financing model to deal with the urgent funding needs of students now trying to access special education, and it is that funding we are calling bridge funding,” she said. The Board Chairperson of the SLTF, Cynthia Amerley Amarteifio, said under the reset agenda of the President, access, inclusion, affordability and sustainability to tertiary education had been placed at the centre of the government’s education agenda.

items.title: Revue de presse de ce jeudi 8 octobre 2026
items.description: Voici les principaux titres développés par la presse nationale de ce jeudi 8 octobre 2026 Al Bayane • La dynamique grandissante de soutien international au plan d’autonomie pour le Sahara marocain a été saluée, mardi au siège des Nations unies, par plusieurs pétitionnaires qui ont souligné que l'initiative marocaine d'autonomie, consacrée par la résolution 2797, a été érigée par le Conseil de sécurité en cadre de référence du processus politique onusien. Selon plusieurs intervenants à cette réunion de la 4e commission, la résolution 2797 du Conseil de sécurité n'a fait que confirmer une dynamique internationale de plus en plus favorable au plan d’autonomie marocain, présenté comme la voie privilégiée pour parvenir à une solution politique durable et mutuellement acceptable au différend artificiel autour du Sahara marocain. • Plusieurs professionnels du secteur des fruits et légumes au Maroc prennent part au Salon « Fruit Attraction » de Madrid, l'un des plus importants évènements internationaux dédiés au secteur agricole, dont la 18è édition se tient du 06 au 08 octobre. Le pavillon marocain, mis en place par Morocco Foodex (établissement autonome de contrôle et de coordination des exportations), abrite 34 exportateurs du secteur représentant l'ensemble des régions du Royaume qui viennent présenter leurs offres aux acheteurs internationaux afin d’explorer de nouvelles opportunités d’affaires au titre de la campagne agricole 2026/2027. • Marsa Maroc poursuit le renforcement de ses équipements au port de Casablanca avec l'arrivée d’une nouvelle grue portuaire Liebherr LPS, une première pour ce modèle sur le continent africain. Installé au terminal polyvalent de Casablanca à la fin du mois de septembre 2026, cet équipement de manutention de type portique pivotant affiche une portée de 48 mètres et une capacité de levage pouvant atteindre 100 tonnes sous crochet. Bayane Al Yaoum • Des participants à une session de formation organisée à Casablanca ont appelé à simplifier les procédures liées à l’autoproduction d’électricité et au raccordement au réseau, ainsi qu’à mettre en place des mesures incitatives en faveur des petits producteurs et des ménages à revenus modestes. L’objectif est d’élargir l’accès à la transition vers les énergies propres, afin qu’elle ne bénéficie pas uniquement aux institutions, aux entreprises et aux ménages disposant des capacités financières nécessaires pour supporter les coûts d’investissement. Ces recommandations ont été formulées lors de la première session de formation consacrée aux méthodes et outils d’évaluation des politiques publiques et des cadres juridiques, organisée les 3 et 4 octobre 2026. Cette rencontre s’inscrit dans le cadre du lancement d’un projet visant à renforcer la gouvernance climatique et à promouvoir une transition énergétique juste au Maroc. • Le président de la Chambre des conseillers, Mohamed Ould Errachid, a mis en avant, à Arusha en Tanzanie, les principales réformes engagées par le Royaume en matière de bonne gouvernance, d'autonomisation des citoyens et de renforcement de leur participation à la gestion de la chose publique. L'instauration d'une relation de confiance plus solide entre le citoyen et les institutions a été au centre du processus de réformes mené par le Maroc, sous le leadership éclairé de Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, qui s'est consolidé avec la Constitution de 2011 ayant consacré les principes de bonne gouvernance, de démocratie citoyenne et participative, d'égalité devant la loi et d'égalité des chances pour tous, a indiqué Ould Errachid lors de la 153e Assemblée générale de l'Union interparlementaire (UIP). • Les opportunités de renforcer la coopération maroco-italienne dans le secteur ferroviaire, à la faveur des grands projets de développement et de modernisation du réseau national, ont été au centre des échanges, à Casablanca, à l'occasion de la Mission entrepreneuriale italienne dédiée aux infrastructures ferroviaires. Réunissant des entreprises italiennes et des acteurs institutionnels et économiques marocains, cette rencontre a permis de mettre en lumière les perspectives de partenariat industriel et technologique entre les deux pays, ainsi que les opportunités offertes par les grands chantiers ferroviaires engagés au Maroc. Al Massae • Le Maroc a accumulé, au cours des deux dernières décennies, des capacités industrielles et technologiques lui permettant de passer à la réalisation des systèmes les plus complexes dans les secteurs de l’aéronautique et de la défense, a affirmé, mercredi à Marrakech, le ministre de l’Industrie et du Commerce, Ryad Mezzour. Intervenant lors de la cérémonie d’ouverture de la 8e édition du Marrakech Air Show, une manifestation placée sous le haut patronage du Roi Mohammed VI, Mezzour a relevé que cette plateforme industrielle, qui n’existait pas il y a 20 ans, est aujourd’hui en mesure de réaliser des systèmes complexes, soulignant que cette dynamique a été rendue possible grâce à la vision clairvoyante du Roi Mohammed VI. • Le ministère de la Santé et de la Protection sociale a exhorté les familles à vérifier que leurs enfants ont bien reçu l'ensemble des doses prévues par le calendrier national de vaccination et à se rendre, si nécessaire, au centre de santé le plus proche pour bénéficier des vaccins requis, conformément aux recommandations et directives en vigueur. Cet appel s'inscrit dans le cadre des efforts déployés par le ministère en vue de renforcer la prévention contre les maladies et de protéger la santé des enfants. Al Ahdat Al Maghribia • Le Maroc, le Fonds Mohammed VI pour l'Investissement (FM6I), BAB Consortium et Recipharm AB ont annoncé la conclusion d'un accord-cadre organisant la cession au Fonds Mohammed VI pour l'Investissement de la participation de 10% détenue par Recipharm dans Maroc Biotechnologies (MARBIO) et le retrait organisé de Recipharm du projet. Cette opération marque l'ouverture d'une nouvelle étape dans le développement de MARBIO, après une première phase consacrée à la structuration, à la mise en place et au démarrage de sa plateforme industrielle de production de vaccins et de produits biologiques au Maroc, indique le FM6I. • Le vice-président de la Chambre des conseillers, Lahcen Haddad, s'est entretenu à Arusha en Tanzanie avec le vice-président du Sénat cambodgien, Ouch Borith, des moyens de renforcer la coopération parlementaire et de développer les relations entre le Maroc et le Cambodge dans plusieurs domaines. Lors de cette rencontre tenue en marge des travaux de la 153e Assemblée générale de l'Union interparlementaire (UIP), M. Haddad a souligné l’importance d'insuffler une nouvelle dynamique aux relations entre le Maroc et le Cambodge, mettant en avant la volonté commune des deux pays de renforcer leurs relations et de tirer profit des atouts qu’offrent la position du Maroc en Afrique et sur la façade atlantique, et celle du Cambodge au sud-est de l’Asie. • Le coup d'envoi de la 8è édition de Marrakech Airshow a été donné, mercredi à la base aérienne des Forces Armées Royales à Marrakech, avec la participation de près de 200 exposants représentant 27 pays dans les domaines de l’aéronautique, de la défense et de l’espace. Le salon constitue une plateforme réunissant les dimensions militaire, industrielle, économique et technologique, offrant aux participants l’occasion d’explorer de nouvelles opportunités de coopération et de nouer des partenariats dans les secteurs de l’aéronautique, de l’espace et de la défense. Cette huitième édition du Marrakech Air Show s’inscrit dans la poursuite du développement de la place du Maroc dans les industries aéronautique et de défense. Assahra almaghribia • Sur Hautes Instructions du Roi, Chef Suprême et Chef d'Etat-Major Général des Forces Armées Royales, le Général de Corps d'Armée, Mohammed Berrid, Inspecteur Général des FAR et Commandant la Zone Sud, a reçu, mardi au niveau du siège de l’Etat-Major Général des FAR à Rabat, le Général de Division Issa Saif Bin Ablan Al Mazrouei, Chef d’Etat-Major des Forces Armées des Émirats Arabes Unis, en visite officielle au Royaume du Maroc, à la tête d'une importante délégation. Lors de cette entrevue, les deux responsables se sont félicités du niveau atteint par la coopération militaire entre les deux pays, notamment dans les domaines de développement capacitaire, d’industrie de défense, de formation ainsi que d’échange d’expériences et d’expertises. Ils ont également réaffirmé leur volonté de poursuivre la consolidation et le développement de cette coopération. • Le Maroc a choisi de développer un modèle industriel ouvert et intégré, profondément ancré en Afrique et relié aux chaînes de valeur mondiales, a indiqué mardi à Rabat la ministre de la Transition énergétique et du Développement durable, Leila Benali. Intervenant à l’Ouverture des travaux de la 3e édition du Congrès International des Mines au Maroc (IMC Morocco 2026), Mme Benali a souligné que ce choix a eu pour objectifs de renforcer l'exploitation minière responsable, d'améliorer la traçabilité, de faciliter l'accès à la finance durable et de soutenir une plus grande création de valeur sur le continent. The post Revue de presse de ce jeudi 8 octobre 2026 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ato Forson says Ghana’s New Economy must create decent jobs for young people
items.description: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson says Ghana’s emerging New Economy must be capable of creating decent and productive jobs on a large scale to give young people a meaningful stake in the country’s future. He said the success of the New Economy should not be measured only by economic growth, but also by its ability to generate sustainable employment opportunities for the country’s growing youth population. Dr Ato Forson made the observation in a Facebook post after engaging academics, researchers and students at the University for Development Studies (UDS), Nyankpala Campus. He described the engagement as “deeply successful and inspiring”, saying the discussions provided an opportunity to exchange ideas on Ghana’s economic future. The Finance Minister said the engagements would continue at the University of Ghana as part of efforts to deepen conversations on the New Economy and its potential to create jobs and expand opportunities for young Ghanaians.

items.title: CAN Maroc 2026 : les Lions de futsal débutent leur quête d'un quadruple sacre inédit
items.description: Le compte à rebours est lancé pour la sélection nationale de futsal. Alors que le coup d'envoi de la Coupe d'Afrique des Nations 2026 approche à grands pas, l'équipe marocaine peaufine les derniers détails de sa préparation au Complexe Mohammed VI de football, portée par la certitude de son statut mais consciente du piège de l'excès de confiance. Triple tenant du titre après ses triomphes en 2016, 2020 et 2024, le Maroc aborde ce rendez-vous continental avec un statut de grandissime favori. Placés dans le groupe A pour ce tournoi qui se déroulera du 12 au 21 octobre au Palais des sports du Complexe Prince Moulay Abdellah de Rabat, les hommes de Hicham Dguig entameront leur parcours face à l'Algérie, avant de croiser le fer avec la Zambie puis la Libye. Au-delà de la rivalité régionale et du cadre de la compétition, l'enjeu dépasse le simple cadre d'une confirmation continentale. Sixièmes au classement mondial de la FIFA, les coéquipiers de Soufiane El Mesrar et Bilal Bakkali se situent désormais dans un registre où l'efficacité tactique et la rigueur physique doivent répondre aux standards des meilleures nations de la discipline, à l'image du Brésil ou du Portugal. Pour l'encadrement technique, ces derniers jours de travail restent axés sur la cohésion tactique, la gestion de la pression à domicile et la fraîcheur physique. Si l'objectif comptable demeure la conquête d'une quatrième couronne africaine successive, cette étape continentale sert également de baromètre pour mesurer la capacité du futsal marocain à maintenir son hégémonie tout en consolidant son ancrage dans l'élite mondiale. The post CAN Maroc 2026 : les Lions de futsal débutent leur quête d'un quadruple sacre inédit appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: India denies bias in satellite internet approvals after Musk's 'oligarchs' jab
items.description: India defended its satellite internet approval process as fair and non-discriminatory on Thursday, hours after billionaire Elon Musk accused unnamed “oligarchs” of blocking Starlink’s ​launch in the South Asian nation. Starlink was being blocked by “certain oligarchs in order ‌to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people,” Musk wrote on X, without naming anyone. India’s telecom market is dominated by billionaires Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Jio and Sunil Mittal’s Bharti Airtel . Their ​satellite internet ventures, alongside Musk’s Starlink, have secured early approvals to launch in ​India but are awaiting spectrum assignment and final clearances. Airtel and Jio ⁠did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The wait has stretched on for four ​years for Starlink, following scrutiny over security requirements and access to spectrum. Responding to Musk’s comments, ​India’s telecommunications ministry said three entities were at broadly the same regulatory stage, with security assessments under way for each. It did not name the companies or Musk. “The suggestion that the framework or ​its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived,” the ministry said in ​a statement. The clash is not new. Musk has previously been at odds with Mittal and Ambani over ‌how India ⁠should grant them spectrum, before the three set aside their differences in 2025 to sign separate deals to distribute Starlink devices in India. India offers Starlink, part of Musk’s SpaceX, access to a satellite broadband market that Deloitte has forecast will be worth $1.9 billion by ​2030. The timing adds a ​diplomatic layer: the ⁠US has pushed Starlink’s market access as a goodwill marker in trade talks with tariff-hit countries , and New Delhi and Washington have struggled to finalise a trade deal since reaching a framework in ​February. Security concerns ⁠have also followed the recovery of Starlink equipment in India. Indian authorities have said they found Starlink devices in two separate operations in late 2024: a drug seizure by police in ⁠the ​Andaman and Nicobar Islands and an army search in ​Manipur state. Musk then said Starlink’s satellite beams were “turned off over India” and were “never on in the first place”, ​a remark he repeated on Wednesday.

items.title: GMTF to equip two Central Region hospitals with advanced diagnostic equipment
items.description: The Ghana Medical Trust Fund (GMTF) is set to strengthen diagnostic services in the Central Region with the provision of advanced medical equipment to the Cape Coast Teaching Hospital and Winneba Trauma and Specialist Hospital. The intervention will see Cape Coast Teaching Hospital receive a 128-slice CT scan, a 1.5 Tesla MRI machine, a 3D mammography system, a stereotactic biopsy system and a fluoroscopy machine. The equipment is expected to expand the hospital’s capacity to diagnose a range of complex medical conditions. At the Winneba Trauma and Specialist Hospital, the GMTF plans to provide a 64-slice CT scan, 3D mammography equipment, a biopsy system, a biochemistry analyser and an ultrasound machine. The initiative was announced during stakeholder engagements in Cape Coast involving traditional rulers, security heads, MMDCEs, academics, students, medical professionals and other stakeholders. The engagements provided an opportunity for the GMTF to outline its mandate and ongoing interventions in the region. The planned investment is aimed at bringing advanced diagnostic services closer to residents, reducing the need for patients to travel long distances for specialised tests and supporting earlier detection of diseases. The GMTF says strengthening diagnostic capacity at the two facilities will ultimately improve access to timely treatment and give more people in the Central Region a better chance of receiving appropriate care when they need it.
