items.title: Tunisie | La marche des diplômés chômeurs se termine en queue de poisson
items.description: Partie le 27 septembre 2026 de Menzel Bouzaiane, dans le gouvernorat de Sidi Bouzid, en direction du palais présidentiel de Carthage, la marche des diplômés chômeurs réclament l'application de la loi n° 18 du 22 décembre 2025 relative au recrutement exceptionnel dans fonction et les entreprises publiques, des diplômés de l’enseignement supérieur restés longtemps sans emploi, s’est terminée en queue de poisson sans que les marcheurs n’aient pu obtenir satisfaction. Latif Belhedi La mobilisation, qui comptait initialement 23 personnes, a progressivement rallié de nouveaux participants en cours de route. Selon le comité de coordination, le nombre de participants a dépassé les 120 personnes, incluant des chômeurs venus d’autres gouvernorats ainsi que des membres de leurs familles ayant choisi de les accompagner. «Nous voulons l ’ application de la loi, pas une rencontre avec le président» , a déclaré à la presse Nesma Mahfoudhi, l’une des coordinatrices de la marche, résumant ainsi la position des participants. Un emploi offert sur un plateau d’argent La revendication porte sur l’ouverture de la plateforme numérique prévue par la réglementation, la définition d’un calendrier de recrutement et le lancement de la première tranche avant la fin de 2026, le recrutement devant se faire sur une période maximale de trois ans et selon des critères prenant notamment en compte l’âge — avec une priorité accordée aux personnes de plus de 40 ans —, l’année d’obtention du diplôme, la situation sociale et le principe d’un seul bénéficiaire par famille. A leur arrivée aux portes de Tunis, après une marche de quelque 300 kilomètres à pieds, marquée par une grande fatigue et des problèmes de santé – plusieurs participants ayant dû recevoir des soins lors des différentes étapes -, les marcheurs ont été empêchés d’avancer davantage et sommés de rentrer au bled les mains vides. L’une des marcheuses, qui s’est montrée intraitable dans la défense de ce qu’elle considère comme un droit, a été arrêtée. «Votre appel a été entendu par le président de la république» , leur a-t-on dit, et des mesures seront prises bientôt pour accélérer l’application de la loi n° 18/2025, qui engage le gouvernement à recruter les diplômés chômeurs par tranches. Mais comme ils se sont lassés des promesses non tenues et qu’ils traînent leur détresse depuis plusieurs années, certains depuis 15 ans et plus, les diplômés chômeurs de Menzel Bouzaiane, l’un des berceaux de la révolution de 2011, rechignent à donner foi à la nouvelle promesse. Et le malaise reste entier. Le malentendu aussi. Car toute cette affaire est né d’un malentendu qu’il va être difficile de lever. En effet, les membres de l’Union des diplômés chômeurs (UDC), qui sont derrière la «Marche de la dignité» , pensent, sans doute à tort, qu’un diplôme ouvre automatiquement la voie à un recrutement dans la fonction publique qui, de ce point de vue, devient un droit inaliénable. Or, on le sait, cela est totalement faux. Un diplôme, quel qu’il soit, est à peine une ligne dans un CV, un indicateur de mérite parmi d’autres. Un emploi ne s’offre pas, il se mérite, par la motivation, le talent, l’expérience et la confiance que l’on inspire à l’employeur. Un diplômé ne doit donc pas dormir sur ses lauriers et attendre un hypothétique emploi dans la fonction publique qui risque de ne jamais venir : son diplôme ne vaut rien s’il n’est pas complété par des formations, des acquis, des savoir-faire… C’est ce que les responsables auraient dû expliquer à ces jeunes diplômé(e)s dont certain(e)s sont presque quinquagénaires. Et non succomber à un populisme de mauvais aloi, dicté par des calculs électoralistes, en leur faisant miroiter la perspective d’un emploi offert sur un plateau d’argent. Tunisie | La marche des diplômés chômeurs reprend après un arrêt à Jelma Une loi populiste qui n’aurait pas dû être promulguée Disons les choses clairement et sans détour : la fameuse loi n° 18/2025, qui a été défendue par tous les partis politiques et les organisations de la société civile, y compris l'UGTT, la centrale ouvrière, et portée par le président Kaïs Saïed, n’aurait jamais dû être promulguée parce qu’elle est inapplicable dans un pays faisant face à une grave crise financière et dont le déficit budgétaire continue de se creuser sur fond d’endettement, intérieur et extérieur, d’inflation structurelle et de croissance économique atone peinant à atteindre 1,5 ou 2 %. Cette loi est d’autant plus inapplicable, également, que la fonction publique en Tunisie emploie plus de 700 000 salariés – là où des pays d’une même grandeur démographique se contenteraient de 200 000 ou 300 000. Près du tiers de ces salariés sont payés d’ailleurs pour ne rien faire, des employés fantômes percevant des salaires fictifs et protestant régulièrement pour exiger des augmentations salariales. Beaucoup d’entre eux ont du reste un second emploi, réel celui-là, dans la contrebande et le marché parallèle qui nuit à l’économie nationale et grève les recettes de l’État par l’évasion fiscale. Au lieu de faire de vagues promesses et de prendre des engagements solennels qu’il n’est pas en mesure de respecter, l’État aurait dû jouer, plus efficacement et avec plus de détermination, le rôle qui est censé être le sien dans la gestion des affaires publiques : mettre en place les conditions requises pour impulser l’investissement, la croissance, la création de richesses et d’emplois, seul moyen pour réduire le déficit budgétaire, l’endettement et le chômage structurel qui touche, bon an mal an, autour de 15% de la population active. A notre connaissance, l’humanité n’a pas inventé d’autres moyens pour sortir du sous-développement, de la pauvreté et de la dépendance de l’aide étrangère qui sont aujourd’hui le lot des Tunisiens soixante-dix ans après leur indépendance. Et c’est dommage… L’article Tunisie | La marche des diplômés chômeurs se termine en queue de poisson est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Major Superiors gather in Wa to chart future of consecrated life
items.description: Leaders of Catholic religious institutes and consecrated men and women from across Ghana have gathered in Wa for a week-long plenary assembly to reflect on the future of consecrated life and strengthen the Church’s mission in a changing society. The Biannual Plenary Assembly of the Conference of Major Superiors of Religious, Ghana (CMSR-Gh), is taking place from 4 to 10 October 2026 at the In-Service Training Centre in the Diocese of Wa. Held under the theme, “Synodal paths to mission sustainability: Walking together in hope”, the assembly brings together religious leaders, consecrated persons and other collaborators for prayer, reflection, dialogue and discernment on their service to the Church and society. Opening the assembly on Tuesday, 6 October, CMSR-Gh President Sr Dr Lucy Hometowu, SMMC, called for stronger collaboration among congregations, saying their different charisms, traditions and apostolates should serve as a source of strength rather than division. “The time has come for us to move beyond simply working alongside one another to genuinely walking together,” she said. Call for greater collaboration Sr Dr Hometowu urged consecrated persons to pool their gifts, experience, personnel and resources to respond more effectively to contemporary challenges. “No single Congregation can respond adequately to all the needs of our time. But when we bring our gifts, experiences, personnel and resources together, we can accomplish much more,” she said. She identified formation, vocation promotion, youth empowerment, safeguarding, ecological justice, healthcare, education, pastoral ministry, social transformation and communication as areas for greater collaboration. Other priorities included caring for elderly and infirm clergy and consecrated persons, as well as managing resources sustainably. She said the CMSR-Gh offered a platform for members to learn from and support one another, while discerning how best to serve the Church and society. Wa Diocese welcomes participants The Bishop of Wa, Most Rev Francis Bomansaan, M.Afr., welcomed participants to the diocese, describing them as co-workers in the vineyard of the Lord. In an address read on his behalf by the Vicar General of the Wa Diocese, Very Rev Fr John Kunpiel, the bishop expressed appreciation for the various charisms and contributions of congregations serving in Ghana. He described the assembly as an opportunity for renewal, reflection on the prophetic and apostolic role of consecrated persons, and stronger collaboration in evangelisation. “This Biannual Conference, my dear brothers and sisters, is more than a meeting. It is a moment of renewal,” he said. Bishop Bomansaan said the theme was timely as the universal Church continued implementing the synodal process. He encouraged participants to practise “working together, listening together, discerning together, and acting together”. He urged them to listen deeply to God and one another during their time in Wa, and to return to their communities with renewed zeal, fresh vision and stronger bonds of fraternity. Mission should outlive its leaders Delivering the keynote address, Franciscan priest and academic Friar Dr Joseph Kwame Blay challenged the Major Superiors to look beyond maintaining existing projects and structures and consider how the Church’s mission could endure beyond the current generation of leaders. He said schools, hospitals, social care institutions and church buildings established by religious institutes were means through which the Church participated in Christ’s mission, rather than the mission itself. “The mission belongs to Christ. We are stewards, collaborators and servants of a mission that precedes us and will outlive us,” he said. Fr Blay explained that a sustainable mission required the transmission of faith, charism, competence and responsibility from one generation to the next. “A mission can have money and still be unsustainable. It can have buildings and still be unsustainable. It can have vocations and still be unsustainable,” he said. He outlined the spiritual, vocational, leadership, institutional, charismatic, financial and material dimensions of sustainability, urging religious institutes to prepare successors deliberately. He warned that a leadership system dependent on one strong individual was fragile and called for a culture that developed people, shared responsibility and prepared the next generation. “The real test of a missionary is not only what happens while he or she is present, but what remains when he or she is gone,” he said. From individual projects to shared mission Fr Blay also called for a shift from an ego-centred approach to mission towards one rooted in Christ and collaboration. He urged religious institutes to strengthen local responsibility, invest in indigenous vocations, develop succession plans, build networks among congregations and explore sustainable economic models without allowing financial considerations to overshadow their mission. He also advocated stronger cooperation between religious institutes and dioceses, saying they had complementary roles in sustaining the Church’s mission. “The question, therefore, should not be: Who owns the mission? But: How can the bishop, diocesan clergy, religious and lay faithful together sustain Christ’s mission entrusted to this local Church?” he said. According to him, the future depended on moving from “mission done for people” to “mission done with people”. The assembly continues until 10 October, with participants reflecting on the challenges and opportunities facing consecrated life and its contribution to the Church in Ghana.

items.title: High school students to turn out for new protests across France
items.description: High school students across France were preparing for a fresh day of protests on Thursday, despite government efforts to ease the crisis which has rocked the country for days. Students have blocked entrances to hundreds of high schools for 15- to 17-year-olds since late September, complaining of missing teachers, overloaded timetables, dilapidated classrooms and buildings that cannot cope with rising temperatures. Student union leaders were urging fresh mobilisation Thursday morning outside high school campuses across France, and in the capital Paris. Protesters face French CRS riot police outside Lycee Helene-Boucher high school as students block the road, during nationwide protests in Paris, France, October 8, 2026, to demand better school conditions. —Reuters National education unions have also called for a general strike Thursday in support of the students. In a televised address on Wednesday evening, the prime minister attempted to calm some of the tensions, promising a plan to respond to the crisis by the end of October. Sebastien Lecornu said that the country could not be “indifferent” to the concerns of high school students, acknowledging that the “anger of young people does not come from nowhere”. He denied that security forces have “orders to confront” the young people, after allegations of excessive police violence. But the students urged the movement to continue. “We want real action, and until we get it, we’ll keep mobilising,” a high school student named Marilou in Fontainebleau told AFP. Suzanne Nijdam, president of student association Fage, said they did not have “even the crumbs of an agreement” after a meeting with the higher education minister Philippe Baptiste. Police officers stand guard as French high school students block the road outside Lycee Helene-Boucher high school, as part of nationwide protests to demand better school conditions in Paris, France, October 8, 2026. —Reuters She called for protests to continue Thursday with “larger-scale demonstrations next week”. The students have asked for a direct meeting with Lecornu to present what they have said are costed proposals to address their demands. Hundreds of students, police and teaching staff have been injured since the protests began, and more than 6,500 people — mostly minors — have been arrested. While many rallies have been peaceful, some demonstrators have started fires, destroyed bus shelters or clashed with riot police. A 15-year-old lost a hand on Monday after police fired a stun grenade, and Interior Minister Laurent Nunez told radio broadcaster RTL early Wednesday that he had suspended the police use of stun grenades in response. Police officers stand guard as French high school students block the road outside Lycee Helene-Boucher high school, as part of nationwide protests to demand better school conditions in Paris, France, October 8, 2026. —Reuters Unions, rights groups and the children have accused the authorities of using disproportionate force, and police have opened 18 internal investigations into allegations of misconduct. The unrest has erupted with just months to go before the 2027 election to choose a successor to centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with far-right veteran candidate Marine Le Pen riding high in the polls despite a graft conviction.

items.title: SIMA 2026 : quatre jours de débats sur l’avenir des médias africains
items.description: La deuxième édition du Salon international des médias d’Afrique (SIMA) s’ouvre ce jeudi 8 octobre au Grand Théâtre Doudou Ndiaye Coumba Rose de Dakar, pour quatre jours d’échanges consacrés aux transformations de l’écosystème médiatique africain. Professionnels des médias, institutions, régulateurs, chercheurs, producteurs de contenus et acteurs technologiques sont attendus autour du thème « Bâtir un écosystème médiatique souverain et performant ». Après une première édition qui avait réuni des représentants de 24 pays africains et enregistré quelque 3 500 présences cumulées aux 14 panels, le SIMA entend franchir un nouveau cap cette année. Les organisateurs annoncent plus de 5 000 participants pour cette deuxième édition, avec une programmation articulée autour de conférences, panels, ateliers, expositions, rencontres professionnelles et sessions de réseautage. La première journée, consacrée à l’économie et aux nouveaux modèles, doit ouvrir les discussions sur l’un des principaux défis auxquels sont confrontés les médias africains : leur viabilité économique. Financement, publicité, monétisation des contenus, diversification des revenus et résilience des entreprises de presse figurent parmi les principaux sujets au programme. L’objectif est notamment de réfléchir aux conditions permettant aux médias de consolider leurs modèles économiques tout en finançant leur transformation. Les travaux se poursuivront vendredi autour des technologies et de l’intelligence artificielle. Les débats porteront notamment sur les usages de l’IA dans les rédactions, la production audiovisuelle, la vérification de l’information, la data et la distribution des contenus. Cette journée intervient dans un contexte marqué par l’accélération de l’introduction des outils d’intelligence artificielle dans les métiers de l’information. Le volet technologique constitue l’un des axes annoncés par les organisateurs pour cette deuxième édition. Lors des préparatifs du salon, le coordonnateur du comité de pilotage, Mactar Silla, avait insisté sur la nécessité pour l’ensemble de l’écosystème médiatique africain – agences de presse, presse écrite, radios, télévisions, influenceurs, producteurs de contenus et industries culturelles et créatives – de réfléchir collectivement aux mutations du secteur. Le samedi 10 octobre sera consacré à la confiance, à l’éthique et à la régulation. Le droit à l’information, la déontologie et la souveraineté des médias seront au cœur des échanges, dans un environnement marqué par l’essor des réseaux sociaux, la circulation massive de contenus et le développement des contenus synthétiques. La dernière journée, dimanche 11 octobre, sera dédiée aux compétences et aux coopérations africaines. Des formations, masterclass, rencontres B2B et échanges professionnels doivent permettre de renforcer les liens entre rédactions, écoles, producteurs, régulateurs et acteurs technologiques. Au-delà des débats, le SIMA veut ainsi favoriser les rencontres entre les différents maillons de la chaîne de l’information. Le salon se présente comme une plateforme destinée à créer des passerelles entre journalistes, éditeurs, producteurs, institutions, créateurs de contenus, écoles et entreprises technologiques. Cette approche doit également favoriser les partenariats et les projets communs à l’échelle du continent. La dimension internationale est également mise en avant. L’Algérie et l’Allemagne ont été désignées pays invités d’honneur, respectivement pour l’Afrique et l’Europe. La présence de délégations étrangères doit contribuer à élargir les échanges entre les professionnels africains et leurs homologues d’autres espaces médiatiques. Pour les organisateurs, l’enjeu dépasse le seul secteur de la presse. Il s’agit de renforcer la capacité des acteurs africains à produire, diffuser et protéger leurs propres contenus et leurs propres récits. Le SIMA prévoit notamment l’élaboration d’une Charte africaine de l’intelligence artificielle dans les médias ainsi que l’adoption d’une Déclaration de Dakar actualisée. Pendant quatre jours, Dakar sera ainsi au centre des discussions sur les mutations économiques, technologiques et professionnelles qui redessinent le paysage médiatique africain. Une rencontre qui entend faire du continent non seulement un espace de consommation de contenus, mais également un acteur de leur production, de leur diffusion et de leur régulation.

items.title: CAN 2025 : Le Maroc et le Sénégal se retrouvent ce jeudi devant le TAS
items.description: Les regards sont tournés ce jeudi vers Lausanne, en Suisse, où le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS) examinera le recours introduit par la Fédération sénégalaise de football contre la décision ayant déclaré le Maroc vainqueur de la finale de la CAN 2025 sur tapis vert, avec un score de 3-0. Cette décision fait suite au retrait des joueurs sénégalais du terrain pendant la rencontre. Cette audience revêt une importance particulière pour le football marocain. Le Royaume s’appuie sur une décision officielle de la commission d’appel de la Confédération africaine de football (CAF), qui a estimé que le départ des joueurs sénégalais constituait une violation des articles 82 et 84 du règlement de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations, entraînant la défaite du Sénégal par trois buts à zéro. La formation arbitrale, composée du Français Gérald Simon, de l’Italien Luigi Fumagalli et de l’Allemand Ulrich Haas, devrait entendre les représentants de la Fédération royale marocaine de football (FRMF), de la Fédération sénégalaise et de la CAF lors d’une audience à huis clos à Lausanne. La finale, disputée le 18 janvier dernier à Rabat, avait été marquée par des événements exceptionnels. Une grande partie des joueurs sénégalais avait quitté la pelouse pour protester contre un penalty accordé au Maroc par l’arbitre dans le temps additionnel. La rencontre avait été interrompue pendant une quinzaine de minutes avant le retour des joueurs sénégalais sur le terrain. Brahim Díaz avait ensuite manqué le penalty marocain, tandis que le Sénégal avait inscrit un but durant la prolongation, s’imposant finalement sur le score de 1-0 au terme du match. La FRMF avait toutefois saisi les instances de la CAF afin de demander l’application des dispositions réglementaires relatives à l’abandon du terrain avant la fin réglementaire d’une rencontre. Le 17 mars dernier, la commission d’appel de la CAF avait décidé de déclarer le Sénégal forfait sur le score de 3-0, en application des articles 82 et 84 du règlement de la compétition, attribuant ainsi la victoire au Maroc. Devant le TAS, le Maroc entend donc défendre une décision déjà rendue par l’instance d’appel de la CAF, tandis que la partie sénégalaise cherche à obtenir son annulation et à faire reconnaître le résultat enregistré sur le terrain. Selon les éléments évoqués autour du dossier, la Fédération sénégalaise fonde notamment son recours sur le principe de la finalité des décisions arbitrales relatives aux faits de jeu. Elle met également en avant le fait que l’arbitre avait autorisé la reprise de la rencontre après le retour des joueurs sénégalais. Au-delà de l’attribution du titre continental, la décision attendue pourrait faire jurisprudence dans le traitement des situations où des joueurs quittent la pelouse pour contester une décision arbitrale. Des spécialistes du droit du sport estiment ainsi qu’une annulation de la sanction prononcée par la CAF, sans justification juridique tenant compte des particularités de cette affaire, pourrait être interprétée comme un précédent susceptible d’encourager les équipes à exercer une pression sur les arbitres en interrompant les rencontres et en provoquant des incidents. À l’inverse, une confirmation de la décision de la CAF renforcerait, selon cette analyse, le principe du respect de l’autorité arbitrale et la nécessité de recourir aux voies réglementaires pour contester une décision, plutôt que d’imposer un rapport de force sur le terrain. The post CAN 2025 : Le Maroc et le Sénégal se retrouvent ce jeudi devant le TAS appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: How Orbih refused Amaechi’s offer to abandon my gov bid – Wike
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has disclosed that the late Chief Daniel Orbih turned down every inducement from the then Governor of Rivers State, Mr Rotimi Amaechi, to withdraw his support for Wike’s governorship ambition. Wike spoke in Abuja on Wednesday at a night of tributes in honour of Orbih, the former National Vice-Chairman (South South) of the Peoples Democratic Party PDP, who died on August 31 at the age of 64. “There was nothing in this world that was not done to induce him. My governor then sent people to Dan, offered him everything in this world, but Dan stood firm and said, ‘No, I will not accept, I will not agree,'” the minister said. Wike traced their bond to the turbulent period between 2013 and 2014, when he said political adversaries made desperate attempts to derail his ambition. “Today I am a Minister of the FCT; yesterday I was a governor. Who did God use for me to become governor? It was Dan,” he said. He said Orbih, as South South National Vice-Chairman of the PDP, backed his campaign by donating two bulletproof Mercedes-Benz buses for his security and mobilising massive structural support across the region. The minister also spoke of Orbih’s selflessness, saying the late politician never sought personal gain, patronage or government contracts throughout Wike’s eight years as governor. “Dan is not a typical Nigerian politician. Throughout my eight years as governor, he never came for one day, either by phone or coming to my house to say, ‘I need this contract.’ Never,” he said. According to Wike, loyalty ran in Orbih’s family. “The only way I can identify a politician that is reliable is when that politician has stood in times of crisis. Loyalty, commitment to friendship, and being a brother’s keeper run in Dan’s family,” he said. Wike stressed that without Orbih’s strength as National Vice-Chairman protecting the region’s interests, many current national and state lawmakers would not have attained their positions. He noted that Orbih laid the foundation for cross-party collaboration in Edo State and supported many politicians there without benefiting from it. He insisted that Orbih deserves a state burial for his contribution to political developments in Edo and urged stakeholders from the state to act on it. “I will continue to keep my relationship with Dan’s family. I think I will also discuss with the family on how to keep the legacies of Dan,” Wike said. Senator Magnus Abe, Chairman of the Board of the Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, said he is a politician today because Orbih introduced him to politics. “I was the Director General of his first campaign in the United Nigeria Congress Party, when he ran for governor and I went everywhere in Edo with him. “Dan was indeed a bridge builder par excellence. We are gathered here today not because Dan is dead. We are gathered because of the life that he lived and that life impacted all of us in so many different ways,” Abe said. Senator Adams Oshiomhole, who represents Edo North in the Senate and is a former Governor of Edo State, said Orbih made him a better governor. “So my happiness today is that Dan and I, whatever our political differences we might have had, the truth is, Dan made me a better governor. “So, when I’m making a decision, the first thing I’ll ask is, ‘If this goes out today, what is Dan Orbih going to say?’ Each time I abstain from doing something because of what the opposition led by Dan will interpret to the people, before I do it will be better prepared. “That is why I say Dan helped me to be a better governor,” he said. He thanked Wike for reuniting him with Orbih after a prolonged political difference. “It was right at Wike’s residence in Port Harcourt that Dan and I started hugging,” Oshiomhole said. Addressing the family, he said: “Please take consolation from the fact that your father built bridges of unity, of progress, and he never did that at the expense of family and he was committed to the growth and development of Ogbona kingdom.” The PDP presidential candidate, Senator Sandy Onor, described Orbih as “a profound public intellectual, a quintessential lover of Edo people, a defender of Edo heritage, a Nigerian patriot and a social colossus.” “Dan was a great man by every measure, a true family man, a great husband, and a worthy father,” he said. items.title: Trump to give Elon Musk top US science medal
items.description: President Donald Trump will present close ally Elon Musk and other tech bosses with the top US scientific award at a ceremony on Thursday, the White House said. Google co-founder Sergei Brin, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and AMD chief Lisa Su will also receive the National Medal of Science at the “Science: A New Golden Age” summit. Computer mogul Michael Dell and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella will get the National Medal of Technology and Innovation, the top award in its field. “The Trump Administration is grateful for the contributions of these incredible leaders in science and technology. These recipients are helping ensure America keeps leading the world in innovation,” White House spokeswoman Liz Huston said in a statement to AFP on Wednesday. Space X and Tesla tycoon Musk has returned to Trump’s good graces after they fell out last year over his role heading the cost-cutting Department of Government Efficiency. He was also the biggest donor to Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign. Musk and Huang were both at Trump’s state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping last month. Along with other tech bosses they were also at the White House last week for talks in which tech chiefs promised to self-regulate against possible threats from artificial intelligence. Trump has dismissed warnings that AI could wipe out humanity, insisting it is crucial for what he calls the “Golden Age” of the US economy in his second term. But Trump’s Republican Party could lose control of Congress in midterm elections next month amid voter concerns over the Iran war and the cost of living. L’accident a suscité plusieurs cris de détresse parmi les populations locales, qui renouvellent leur demande d’installation de ralentisseurs sur cet axe traversant la commune. Le drame s’est produit aux environs de 17 heures. Selon les informations recueillies sur place, l’ambulance revenait de Tambacounda en direction de Bakel lorsqu’elle a heurté l’enfant. La victime, A. Cissakho n’a pas survécu à ses blessures. Cet accident relance les préoccupations exprimées depuis plusieurs années par les habitants de Goudiry sur la sécurité de la circulation au niveau de la RN1. Plusieurs voix se sont élevées à la suite du drame pour demander la mise en place de dispositifs destinés à réduire la vitesse des véhicules dans les zones à forte fréquentation. La RN1 traverse la commune et longe notamment des établissements et services fréquentés quotidiennement par les populations, parmi lesquels des écoles, le district sanitaire, la gendarmerie et le tribunal. Cette configuration expose les piétons, notamment les enfants et les personnes se rendant dans les structures sanitaires, aux risques liés à la circulation sur cet axe national. La demande de ralentisseurs intervient également dans un contexte marqué par d’autres accidents mortels enregistrés dans la commune. Des habitants évoquent notamment le décès récent d’un autre enfant dans des circonstances liées à la circulation sur la RN1. Dans une lettre ouverte adressée aux autorités, Alhousseynou Bassoum, chargé de mission à la Présidence de la République et coordonnateur départemental de la JPS de Goudiry, a récemment alerté sur la situation sécuritaire autour de cet axe. Il appelle notamment à l’installation de ralentisseurs conformes aux normes, au renforcement de la signalisation et à la matérialisation de passages piétons. La correspondance préconise également l’installation de panneaux indiquant les zones scolaires et sanitaires, le renforcement des contrôles de vitesse ainsi que l’amélioration de l’éclairage public. Elle demande, plus largement, la réalisation d’un diagnostic de sécurité routière sur les portions de la RN1 traversant les zones fortement fréquentées de Goudiry. Après le décès d’A. Cissakho, ces revendications sont de nouveau exprimées par des habitants qui souhaitent voir renforcer les dispositifs de sécurité routière sur la traversée de la commune.

items.title: ECG warns customers against fake meter sales, MoMo fraud
items.description: The Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) has warned customers across the country against fraudsters posing as its staff or agents to sell fake meters and demand payments through personal mobile money accounts. The company says customers should not send money to private MoMo numbers for electricity services. ECG General Manager for External Communications, Dr Charles Nii Ayiku Ayiku, said the company operates a fully cashless payment system, with customers required to make payments through official channels. “ECG runs a fully cashless system,” Dr Ayiku said. “All payments must go through the ECG Power App or the shortcode *226#. Money sent to a personal MoMo number does not reach the company and will not reflect on your account.” Dr Ayiku identified the sale of meters by individuals as one of the schemes being used to defraud customers. He said some individuals pose as ECG staff or agents and offer to supply and install new meters for a fee. Others advertise meters on WhatsApp and social media platforms, including TikTok, before asking customers to make payments. In some cases, customers receive unregistered meters which ECG may treat as an illegal connection. “ECG does not sell meters through individuals,” he said. He urged customers seeking new meters or electricity services to use official ECG channels, including district offices and the ECG Power App, and to pay only approved fees through the company’s official payment platforms. The second scheme involves phone calls from individuals claiming to be ECG staff. According to Dr Ayiku, the caller may tell a customer that their meter is ready and then provide a personal MoMo number for payment. “Our staff does not ask customers to pay into personal mobile money wallets,” he said. “Treat any such call as a fraud attempt.” He said the fraudsters often rely on urgency to pressure customers into making payments before verifying the information. Dr Ayiku urged customers to take time to confirm any request purportedly coming from ECG before making a payment. He advised customers to: Never send money to a personal MoMo number provided by someone claiming to be an ECG employee. Avoid buying meters from individuals, online adverts or WhatsApp contacts. Make electricity payments only through the ECG Power App or *226#. Keep PINs, passwords and verification codes confidential. Ask anyone visiting their home or business on behalf of ECG to produce a valid staff identification card. End suspicious calls and report the number to ECG and the police. “Pay only through the ECG Power App or *226#,” Dr Ayiku said. “Treat all other payment requests as fraud and report them.”

items.title: I don’t want my children’s English identity questioned – Badenoch
items.description: Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch has defended the British identity of her mixed-race children, saying she does not want to live in a country where their English identity is questioned. Badenoch, MP for North West Essex, made the remarks during her speech at the Conservative Party Conference 2026 on Wednesday, while criticising Reform UK MPs over what she described as attempts to question people’s identities. “I don’t want to live in a country run by people who threaten journalists, who call veterans traitors, and debate whether my mixed-race children are English,” she said. “I don’t want to explain to my son when we’re watching our brilliant England team play football that some people don’t think our black players are English,” she said. She recalled former England internationals Ian Wright and John Barnes, saying their English identity was not questioned in the same way. “I remember back in the day when Ian Wright and John Barnes were playing, nobody was questioning whether they were English,” Badenoch said. “We certainly didn’t have sitting MPs questioning whether they were English,” she added. Badenoch warned against what she described as attempts to take Britain backwards, saying the country should not accept such divisions. “We must not let these people take us backwards. That is not the country we are,” she said. She also accused Reform UK MPs of openly questioning people’s identities, drawing a distinction between the party and the Conservatives. “Reform MPs are openly questioning people’s identity. They are not like us. We are not like them,” Badenoch said. “We are different. We are the Conservative Party,” she added. items.title: 2027: Gov Yusuf reconciles Deputy Senate President Barau, Bichi
items.description: Gov. Abba Yusuf of Kano State has reconciled Deputy Senate President, Barau Jibrin, and a member of the House of Representatives, Abubakar Bichi, ahead of the 2027 general elections. This is contained in a statement by the governor’s media aide, Sanusi Bature, on Wednesday in Kano. Bature said that the governor facilitated the reconciliation meeting which lasted for two hours on Tuesday in Abuja. He said that the meeting provided an opportunity for the two prominent APC leaders to address their differences and discuss the need to work together for the collective interest of the party. Barau represented Kano-North Senatorial District, while Bichi represented Bichi Federal Constituency, and Chairman House Committee on Appropriations. The statement quoted the governor as urging the two political leaders and their supporters to bury their differences and grievances. According to Yusuf, the success of the APC requires unity, mutual understanding and collective commitment among its leaders and members. He underscored the importance of working together for the success of President Bola Tinubu and all the APC candidates in the elections. The governor urged party members to put the overall interest of the party above individual differences. “Political disagreements are part of democratic engagement, but such differences should not be allowed to undermine the unity, stability and progress of the party,” Yusuf was quoted as saying in the statement. Yusuf stressed that the APC remained one family, adding all stakeholders have a responsibility to resolve internal crises through dialogue, consultation and mutual respect. He enjoined supporters of the two leaders to embrace reconciliation, avoid inflammatory statements, character assassination and acts capable of promoting disuniting in the party. Yusuf expressed confidence that the reconciliation would contribute to greater unity among APC members, and strengthen its collective efforts ahead of the 2027 general elections. “Henceforth, I do not expect any of your supporters to come out and abuse one another. We must put a stop to these unnecessary distractions. “The APC is set to win all elective positions in Kano come 2027 by God’s Grace,” Yusuf said. The statement also quoted Barau and Bichi, as warning their supporters against fueling internal conflicts within the party in the state. They assured their continued support, loyalty and commitment toward the success of the party at the poll in the state. (NAN) The post 2027: Gov Yusuf reconciles Deputy Senate President Barau, Bichi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Gombe NBA accuses AIG of extortion, police chief denies allegation
items.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Gombe Branch, has called for an investigation into allegations of extortion, intimidation and unprofessional conduct levelled against the Assistant Inspector-General of Police (AIG), Force Criminal Investigation Department (FCID) Annex, Gombe, Emmanuel Agene. The NBA also urged the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Tunji Disu, to investigate the allegations and take appropriate action if they are established. Chairman of the Gombe NBA, Barrister Alhassan Mu’azu, made the call on Wednesday evening after the branch’s monthly congress attended by lawyers, elders and past leaders of the association in Gombe. Mu’azu said the allegations followed a complaint by a member of the branch, Barrister E.S. Tizhe, who represented Ahmed Shuaibu Gara in a matter being investigated at the FCID Annex over an allegation of cyberbullying. According to him, Tizhe had gone to the police facility to represent his client in accordance with the constitutional right of a person under investigation to legal representation. Mu’azu cited Section 36 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which guarantees the right to counsel in criminal proceedings. He alleged that money was demanded as a condition for Gara’s release on bail, describing such a demand, if established, as unlawful and unconstitutional. The NBA chairman said the branch subsequently constituted a committee comprising senior members and elders to examine complaints concerning activities at the FCID Annex. “We have been gathering information. It is not only that of Tizhe. The branch had to constitute a committee of bar leaders and elders of the branch to investigate the activities and alleged extortion that is ongoing,” he said. Mu’azu said the committee had received information from other persons who allegedly had similar experiences and was preparing its report for submission to the appropriate authorities. He further alleged that some lawyers had been subjected to embarrassing treatment while representing their clients at the police facility, insisting that the NBA would not remain silent if the allegations were substantiated. “We are condemning this in the strongest terms. We are calling on the Inspector-General of Police to ensure that these activities are properly investigated and that the AIG, if found wanting, must be prosecuted,” he said. The NBA chairman said the branch was prepared to present whatever evidence it had to the police authorities or any competent investigative body. He also disclosed that Tizhe had petitioned the IGP over the matter and that the petition was subsequently referred to the AIG for his response. Mu’azu alleged that following the petition, Agene contacted him and asked him to appear before him. “The AIG kept calling me as the chairman of the branch that I should come, as if he wanted to arrest me. That is wrong,” he alleged. He said the NBA was awaiting the outcome of the IGP’s consideration of the petition, adding that the association could seek judicial redress if it was dissatisfied with the handling of the matter. “If the Inspector-General of Police is not taking action, we are going to join hands with our President of the Nigerian Bar Association. “We are going to ensure that we sue not only the AIG FCID Annex, but, if no action is taken, the entire Nigerian Police Force, including the Police Service Commission,” he said. Lawyer alleges N700,000 payments In his petition to the IGP dated September 7, 2026, Tizhe of Habu Abdu & Co. alleged that his client was arrested on August 14, 2026, following a complaint involving alleged criminal mischief and criminal defamation of character. The lawyer alleged that after his client’s statement was obtained, they were taken to the AIG’s office, where, he claimed, money was demanded for the suspect’s release. According to the petition, the AIG allegedly told him that his client would be granted bail and asked the suspect to “drop some money.” Tizhe alleged that his client initially paid ₦100,000. He further alleged that he was asked to submit his Call to Bar certificate and NBA identification card as part of the bail process. The lawyer said that after a surety was produced, he returned to collect the documents but alleged that they were not immediately released to him. Tizhe also alleged that his client was asked to pay another ₦100,000 on August 17, while he personally paid ₦500,000 on August 20 following what he described as threats. The petition further alleged that complainants seeking investigation of criminal complaints at the FCID Annex were sometimes required to pay between ₦50,000 and ₦100,000 before investigations could commence. Tizhe consequently asked the IGP to intervene and investigate what he described as alleged extortion at the FCID Annex, Gombe. AIG denies allegations Responding to the petition, however, AIG Agene denied demanding or receiving money from Gara, his surety or the lawyer. In a letter dated October 2, 2026, addressed to the IGP, Agene said the case involved an allegation of cyberbullying against Gara, adding that the suspect had made a statement during the investigation. The AIG said the lawyer subsequently requested administrative bail for his client and that the conditions for bail were communicated to the parties. He explained that the lawyer initially offered to stand as surety for the suspect but was informed that, as the suspect’s solicitor, he could not act as surety. According to him, the lawyer later produced a police auditor, Usman Adamu, as surety. Agene said he directed the lawyer to indicate that he knew the proposed surety and provide his Call to Bar certificate and identification card to facilitate the suspect’s production when required. He maintained that the documents were voluntarily submitted and denied that their submission was connected to any demand for money. “The AIG Force CID Annex Gombe neither had discussion of any money and/or received same from both the suspect, the surety and the solicitor,” Agene stated. He challenged the lawyer to produce evidence to substantiate the allegation that money was demanded or collected. The AIG also alleged that investigators subsequently had difficulty reaching the surety after the suspect’s release. Agene further accused the lawyer and the suspect of attempting to use social media to intimidate persons in pursuit of financial compensation, alleging that similar accusations had previously been made against the FCID Annex in 2025. He described the extortion allegation as an attempt to tarnish his reputation and questioned why he would demand ₦50,000, as alleged, after years of service in the police force. Agene insisted that he neither demanded nor received money from the suspect, the surety or the lawyer. He also asked the lawyer to appear with the suspect and surety for the continuation of the investigation. The AIG further warned that the lawyer could face legal action over alleged obstruction of an offender and defamation of character if the matter was not resolved. The allegations made by the NBA and the lawyer have not been judicially established, while the AIG has expressly denied wrongdoing. The matter remains subject to any investigation or other lawful proceedings that may follow. The post Gombe NBA accuses AIG of extortion, police chief denies allegation appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: SERAP challenges ₦100m DSS defamation award at appeal court
items.description: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has urged the Court of Appeal sitting in Abuja to set aside the judgment of the Federal Capital Territory High Court awarding ₦100 million in damages against SERAP in a defamation suit brought by two officers of Nigeria’s State Security Service (SSS). The appeal is scheduled for hearing on Friday. The appeal, filed by SERAP following the judgment delivered by Justice Yusuf Halilu on 5 May 2026, challenges the findings of liability, the award of damages and the consequential orders, including the order requiring SERAP to publish an apology. The Appellant’s Brief of Argument, dated 3 September 2026 and filed at the Court of Appeal by SERAP’s counsel, Tayo Oyetibo, SAN, is based on 24 grounds and raises important questions concerning the essential elements of defamation, the evidential burden of establishing identification, the competence of the evidence relied upon by the trial Court, and the protection of freedom of expression and public-interest advocacy. SERAP said: “The central issue in this appeal is whether the respondents established by credible evidence that the publications complained of referred to them. The publications did not name the respondents, and the descriptions relied upon were general physical descriptions which did not, without more, identify the particular individuals who brought the action.” The lawsuit arose after SERAP published an account on 9 September 2024 alleging that DSS officers had unlawfully entered its Abuja office, following the organisation’s call on President Bola Tinubu to investigate allegations of corruption at the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) and reverse fuel price increases. The publications referred to officers from the SSS/DSS and described them, among other things, as “a tall, large, dark-skinned woman” and “a slim, dark-skinned man”. The officers were not named in the publications. SERAP’s Brief of Argument reads in part: “The alleged suspension of the 1st and 2nd Respondents was likewise not supported by independent documentary evidence. The award against SERAP was therefore not only excessive but also arbitrary and ought to be set aside.” “The learned trial Judge relied, inter alia, on assertions that the publication had affected the 1st and 2nd Respondents ‘mentally and psychologically’ and had ‘gone viral’, without sufficient evidence establishing the extent of the publication or any specific professional, financial or reputational injury suffered by the Respondents.” “The award of liability cannot stand where the essential findings on falsity and justification were not supported by the evidence We respectfully submit that the finding of liability and consequential award of damages cannot stand once the findings upon which they were founded are shown to be erroneous.” “Where a claimant is not expressly named in a publication, the burden remains on the claimant to establish by evidence the circumstances from which a reasonable reader would understand the publication to refer specifically to that claimant. That essential link was not established in this case.” “Neither publication identified the respondents by name, rank, designation, office or photograph. The descriptions relied upon were physical descriptions which, on the evidence before the trial Court, were not unique to the respondents.” “The respondents pleaded that members of the public and persons within the SSS understood the publications to refer to them, but no member of the public was called to testify that they had read the publications and understood them to refer to the respondents.” “No independent witness was called to establish the alleged identification, while the social-media reactions relied upon by the respondents were not tendered in evidence.” “The law is settled that the words complained of in an action for defamation must be considered from the standpoint of the ordinary reasonable reader. The question is whether a reasonable person reading the publication would associate the words complained of with the claimant.” “The significance of this principle in the present appeal is considerable. The two SSS/DSS officers were not named in either publication. Their case therefore depended upon establishing by evidence the factual circumstances connecting the descriptions contained in the publications to their particular identities.” “The trial Court consequently supplied the missing identifying link by relying, among other things, on its own observation of the physical appearance of the respondents in Court.” “The trial Court could not properly supply by its own observation the essential identifying link which the respondents were required to establish by evidence. The issue was whether the publications identified the respondents when they were published, not whether the respondents happened to fit the descriptions when they appeared before the Court.” “The respondents instituted this action at the trial Court by initially filing a Writ of Summons against the Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project, a non-juristic person. The respondents subsequently amended their Writ of Summons to substitute the said non-juristic entity with the Incorporated Trustees of the Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project.” “An action commenced against a non-juristic person is fundamentally defective and does not constitute a misnomer which is capable of amendment. An amendment cannot cure a void originating process nor effect the substitution of a distinct juristic entity for a party that does not exist in law.” “The evidence before the trial Court established that the first respondent signed her witness statement at her lawyers’ chambers rather than before a Commissioner for Oaths. The statutory requirements governing the administration and execution of an oath are not matters of mere formality.” “A witness statement on oath which was not properly sworn cannot be retrospectively validated simply because the witness subsequently adopted the statement in open Court. Adoption cannot cure a fundamental defect in the manner in which the statement was sworn.” “There is no such ambiguity here. The present case is materially different and the authority relied upon does not justify the learned trial Judge’s failure to properly consider the first respondent’s admission concerning the execution of her witness statement on oath.” “The publications ought to have been read as a whole and in their proper factual and contextual setting. Particular words and expressions, including ‘invasion’, ‘harassment’, ‘intimidation’ and ‘unlawful’, should not have been isolated from the facts and circumstances giving rise to the publications.” “The publications concerned the conduct of State security officials who visited SERAP’s Abuja office without prior notice, sought access to staff and management, and whose presence generated concerns and interactions with SERAP staff.” “SERAP’s assessment and characterisation of those events constituted comment on a matter of legitimate public interest. The fact that the respondents disagreed with that characterisation does not, without more, establish defamation.” “SERAP had established the factual foundation for the publications, and the evidence before the trial Court did not establish that the substance of the publications was false. The respondents could not succeed merely by demonstrating that they disagreed with SERAP’s account or characterisation of the events.” “Qualified privilege may be defeated by proof of express or actual malice. No such evidence was established. Mere disagreement with the Appellant’s account does not, without more, establish malice.” “Section 39(1) protects the freedom to hold opinions and to impart information and ideas. That protection is particularly important for civil society organisations whose work necessarily involves scrutinising public institutions and commenting on matters affecting human rights, accountability and the rule of law.” “Officers of a public security agency do not, by virtue of their office, become immune from legitimate criticism concerning the manner in which public functions are performed.” “The right to comment freely on matters of public interest is one of the fundamental rights of free speech guaranteed to the individual in our Constitution.” “The protection of reputation and the protection of freedom of expression must be carefully balanced. That balance is particularly important where the speech concerns the conduct of security agencies and other public authorities.” “The trial Court failed to consider the defences relied upon by the Appellant which were factually and legally available to the Appellant. The imposition of liability and award of outrageous damages were not supported by the evidence led in Court.” “The suit of the 1st and 2nd Respondents was frivolous, vexatious and lacked merit given that the publications in question, as shown in Exhibit D2, were made against the SSS as an institution, yet the two unidentified 1st and 2nd Respondents filed this suit in their personal capacities.” “The central issue in this appeal is whether the essential elements of defamation were established by evidence and whether legitimate public-interest criticism can properly be transformed into personal liability without satisfying those requirements.” “The finding of liability and consequential award of damages cannot stand once the findings upon which they were founded are shown to be erroneous. The learned trial Judge misdirected himself on identification, the meaning of the publications, falsity and the Appellant’s defences.” “SERAP remains committed to lawful and evidence-based advocacy on matters affecting human rights, accountability and the rule of law. Civil society organisations must be able to scrutinise and comment on the conduct of public institutions without the threat of disproportionate legal consequences.” “We urge the Court of Appeal to uphold the requirements of due process and the constitutional protection of freedom of expression and to set aside the judgment and consequential orders challenged in this appeal.” The post SERAP challenges ₦100m DSS defamation award at appeal court appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 9 terrorists killed in North Waziristan IBO: state media
items.description: Security forces killed nine terrorists in an intelligence-based operation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan, state media reported on Wednesday. According to state-run Pakistan TV , IBOs were carried out in several areas of North Waziristan, including Palangzai, Nadeem Kot, and Kot Khazri, eliminating nine Fitna al-Khwarij terrorists, including four “important terrorist commanders”. Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). It added that several hideouts were destroyed and a large quantity of weapons and ammunition was recovered from the slain terrorists. President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif commended security forces for their successful operation, state-run APP reported. In a statement, the president said the elimination of nine terrorists was a manifestation of the professional capability and bravery of the security forces. He emphasised that every conspiracy by the foreign patrons of terrorists and their local facilitators would be thwarted. In his statement, PM Shehbaz said the successful operations reflected Pakistan’s unwavering resolve to completely eliminate terrorism from the country. The prime minister lauded the officers and personnel of the security forces for their commendable services and sacrifices to eradicate terrorism. He reiterated the government’s resolve to foil the nefarious designs of terrorists seeking to create unrest and undermine peace and stability in the country. KP has long faced security challenges. In August , the province, excluding the merged districts, recorded 54 terrorist attacks compared with 36 in July, representing an increase of 50 per cent, according to data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS). A day earlier, security forces killed 13 terrorists in another IBO in North Waziristan. On Tuesday, in yet another North Waziristan IBO, security forces killed five terrorists, state media said, while seven were killed on October 2. On September 30, security forces killed three terrorists in an IBO in Mir Ali. A day before that, in an IBO in the Bara area, security forces killed five terrorists. On Sept 28, four terrorists were killed during an IBO in Dera Ismail Khan. On Sept 26, a dozen people lost their lives while 35 others were injured in a suicide blast that targeted the Aman Mela police checkpost in DI Khan’s Darazinda tehsil. On Sept 18, a major attack in the old Police Lines in Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation . On Sept 17, security forces killed 10 terrorists in separate operations in KP between Sept 15 and 17. Earlier that month, over 20 terrorists were killed during multiple engagements in KP between Sept 3 and 5.

items.title: God used Dan Orbih to make me Rivers governor — Wike
items.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, has recounted how late Chief Daniel Orbih served as the divine instrument that paved the way for his emergence as Rivera governor in 2015. Wike made the disclosure in Abuja on Wednesday, during a night of tributes in honour of Orbih, the National Vice-Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), South South. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Orbih, from Etsako in Edo State died on Aug. 31 at 64. Wike revealed the high-stakes political intrigues, extreme pressure, and financial inducements that Orbih, widely known as simply Dan, resisted to remain steadfast in supporting his gubernatorial ambition. He traced the roots of their close bond to the critical political period between 2013 and 2014, describing it as a turbulent era where political adversaries made desperate attempts to derail his ambition. “Today I am a Minister of the FCT; yesterday I was a governor. Who did God use for me to become governor? It was Dan,” Wike said. Recalling the intense pressure mounted by opponents, including the sitting governor of Rivers at the time, Wike disclosed that massive inducements were offered to Orbih to withdraw his support, but he firmly refused. “There was nothing in this world that was not done to induce him. My governor then sent people to Dan, offered him everything in this world, but Dan stood firm and said, ‘No, I will not accept, I will not agree.’ The minister said that as the South South National Vice-Chairman of the PDP, Orbih backed his campaign by donating two bulletproof Mercedes-Benz buses to strengthen his security and mobilised massive structural support across the region. Wike expressed profound admiration for Orbih’s rare selflessness, pointing out that throughout his eight-year tenure as Governor of Rivers, Orbih never sought personal gain, patronage, or government contracts. “Dan is not a typical Nigerian politician. Throughout my eight years as governor, he never came for one day—either by phone or coming to my house to say, ‘I need this contract.’ Never,” he said. He added that the loyalty and commitment demonstrated by Orbih were traits deeply rooted in his family heritage. “The only way I can identify a politician that is reliable is when that politician has stood in times of crisis. Loyalty, commitment to friendship, and being a brother’s keeper run in Dan’s family,” he said. Wike stressed that without Orbih’s strength as National Vice-Chairman in the South South protecting the region’s interests, many current national and state lawmakers would not have attained their positions today. Highlighting Orbih’s strategic foresight, Wike noted that the late political titan laid the foundation for cross-party collaboration in Edo and supported many politicians in the state but had not benefited from it. The FCT minister insisted that Orbih deserves a state burial, considering his contribution to the political developments in Edo and urged stakeholders in the state to do something about it. He promised to maintain a strong relationship with the deceased family and discuss how to keep Orbih’s legacies. Also, Sen. Magnus Abe, Chairman of the Board of the Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, also disclosed that he is a politician today because of Orbih explaining that it was the deceased that introduced him to politics. “I was the Director General of his first campaign in the United Nigeria Congress Party, when he ran for governor and I went everywhere in Edo with him. “Dan was indeed a bridge builder par excellence. We are gathered here today not because Dan is dead. We are gathered because of the life that he lived and that life impacted all of us in so many different ways,” he said. On his part, Sen. Adams Oshiohomle, representing Edo North in the Senate and former Governor of Edo, said that Orbih made him a better governor. “So my happiness today is that Dan and I, whatever our political differences we might have had, the truth is, Dan made me a better governor. “So, when I’m making a decision, the first thing I’ll ask is, ‘If this goes out today, what is Dan Orbih going to say?’ Each time I abstain from doing something because of what the opposition led by Dan will interpret to the people, before I do it will be better prepared. “That is why I say Dan helped me to be a better governor,” he said. To the family, Oshiohomle said, “please take consolation from the fact that your father built bridges of unity, of progress, and he never did that at the expense of family and he was committed to the growth and development of hisnxommunity. He thanked Wike for reuniting him and Orbih after a prolonged political difference saying, “it was right at Wike’s residence in Port Harcourt that Dan and I started hugging”. In his tribute, PDP presidential candidate, Sen. Sandy Onor, described Orbih as “a profound public intellectual, a quintessential lover of Edo people, a defender of Edo heritage, a Nigerian patriot and a social colossus. “Dan was a great man by every measure, a true family man, a great husband, and a worthy father,” he said. (NAN) The post God used Dan Orbih to make me Rivers governor — Wike appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sénégal-Rwanda : onze accords pour élargir la coopération bilatérale
items.description: Le Sénégal et le Rwanda ont conclu onze accords et instruments de coopération dans plusieurs domaines, à l’issue de la session inaugurale de leur Grande Commission mixte de coopération, tenue les 6 et 7 octobre à Kigali. Cette rencontre, conduite côté sénégalais par le ministre de l’Intégration africaine, des Affaires étrangères et des Sénégalais de l’Extérieur, Cheikh Niang, ouvre une nouvelle étape dans le renforcement des relations entre Dakar et Kigali. Les onze instruments signés couvrent notamment les consultations politiques, les technologies de l’information et de la communication (TIC), l’innovation, le tourisme, la jeunesse, la culture et les arts, le sport, l’enseignement supérieur, la recherche scientifique et la normalisation. Trois accords portent, pour leur part, sur l’entraide judiciaire en matière pénale, l’extradition et le transfèrement des personnes condamnées. La session a permis aux deux délégations d’examiner l’état de la coopération bilatérale et d’identifier de nouveaux secteurs susceptibles de faire l’objet de partenariats. Au-delà des domaines couverts par les accords conclus, Dakar et Kigali entendent notamment approfondir leurs échanges dans la défense et la sécurité, l’éducation, l’économie, les infrastructures, le numérique, l’agriculture, la santé, le tourisme et les investissements. Pour le ministre rwandais des Affaires étrangères et de la Coopération internationale, Olivier Nduhungirehe, l’enjeu est désormais de traduire les engagements politiques en résultats concrets. Il a notamment insisté sur la nécessité d’assurer la mise en œuvre effective des accords conclus, au bénéfice des deux pays. Le ministre Cheikh Niang a, dans le même sens, souligné l’importance du suivi et de la concrétisation des engagements pris. La dimension économique a occupé une place importante dans les échanges. En marge de la Grande Commission mixte, le Forum des Affaires et des Investissements Rwanda-Sénégal a réuni des représentants des secteurs public et privé des deux pays. Organisée avec l’appui de l’Agence sénégalaise de promotion des investissements et des grands travaux (APIX) et du Rwanda Development Board (RDB), cette rencontre a porté sur les possibilités de partenariats, le développement des échanges commerciaux et la promotion des investissements. Le forum vise ainsi à rapprocher davantage les milieux d’affaires des deux pays. Les discussions ont notamment porté sur les opportunités de collaboration et d’investissement, avec l’ambition de donner une traduction économique aux relations politiques entre Dakar et Kigali. Le Rwanda et le Sénégal entendent également s’appuyer sur la Zone de libre-échange continentale africaine (ZLECAf) pour accroître les échanges et les investissements intra-africains. Cette nouvelle séquence de coopération intervient après la visite d’État de trois jours effectuée par le président Bassirou Diomaye Faye au Rwanda en octobre 2025. À cette occasion, Dakar et Kigali avaient déjà conclu plusieurs accords portant notamment sur la mobilité, l’agriculture et l’élevage, la santé, la planification du développement et les services pénitentiaires. Les deux pays avaient également acté des mesures relatives à la circulation des détenteurs de différents types de passeports. Pour assurer le suivi des engagements issus de la session de Kigali, les deux parties ont décidé de mettre en place un comité conjoint chargé de veiller à la mise en œuvre des décisions et recommandations adoptées. Une réunion d’experts est également prévue en 2027 pour évaluer les progrès réalisés. La deuxième session de la Grande Commission mixte devrait se tenir au Sénégal, à une date qui sera fixée par voie diplomatique.

Saudi says three dead in airport attacks claimed by Houthis
items.description: Saudi authorities said Wednesday three people were killed in attacks on two of the kingdom’s international airports, including in the capital Riyadh, after Yemen’s Houthis claimed to have fired on both transport hubs. The Iran-backed Houthis have claimed a wave of attacks on Saudi civilian infrastructure in recent weeks, which came as Riyadh-backed forces pressed a counter-offensive against the group’s territorial gains. Since Yemen’s civil war reignited in July, more than 200,000 people have been displaced within the country, the United Nations said Wednesday. The Houthis claimed an attack on Riyadh’s main airport, while the Saudi-led coalition — which backs Yemen’s internationally recognised government in its fight against the group — vowed retaliation. The Houthis later claimed another attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on Thursday and repeated a warning — “for the last time” — to airlines to avoid Saudi airspace. “On Tuesday and Wednesday… Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport were subjected to attacks targeting their facilities,” Saudi Arabia’s civil aviation authority said in a statement. An Egyptian and an Algerian national were killed at Abha airport, while a Sudanese national was killed at Riyadh airport, the agency said. The attacks wounded 36 people, it added. In a subsequent statement, the coalition directly blamed Houthi fighters for the strikes and vowed a response. “The brutal attacks by the Terrorist Houthi Militia on civilian and civilian objects in the Kingdom, most recently targeting (the two airports) will not go unpunished,” it wrote on X. The coalition said it had retaliated by striking 82 “legitimate military targets”, including missile facilities, command centres, communications systems and Houthi gathering sites. Yemen’s government declared a major counter-offensive against the Houthis this week, claiming to have pushed the fighters out of strategic areas on the Red Sea and the port city of Mocha. But the Houthis insist they are holding their territory, and military sources from both sides contacted by AFP have not reported any major changes on the ground. Claims by the warring parties have been impossible to independently verify with the situation moving fast and access for journalists difficult. – Flight diverted – Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said Wednesday that the group had targeted Riyadh’s airport in an “accurate” strike that “led to a disruption of air traffic.” The Saudi-led military coalition said on X it “destroyed the ballistic missile launch platform” used in the attack. The Houthis also said they targeted a military supply convoy near the airport in Aden, the interim capital for Yemen’s government. The government’s Saba news agency reported missiles and drones targeting that airport. The agency cited transport authorities as saying one of the missiles landed near the runway minutes before the scheduled arrival of a flight from Cairo, which was forced to divert to Jeddah in Saudi Arabia. Houthi drones and missiles also targeted Saudi Arabia’s Abha airport and King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait, Houthi spokesman Saree said, claiming they had “hit their targets accurately”. It is the second time this week Houthis claimed to have attacked Riyadh’s main airport. – ‘Terrified’ – Saudi Arabia has led an international coalition fighting the Houthis since 2015, and is now trying to roll back the group’s latest advance. The coalition said Monday it was providing air support for the Yemeni government’s counter-offensive. After four years of ceasefire, the Houthis claimed last month they had seized Yemen’s entire western coastline along the Red Sea in the country’s deadliest fighting in years. New clashes on Wednesday in Yemen’s west left at least 62 combatants dead, including 37 Houthis, military sources from both camps told AFP. Saba also reported that a Houthi missile wounded five civilians in Taiz, a city held by government forces. “We went out into the street to check on the wounded and saw young civilians who had been hit,” resident Al-Fateh al-Eisaei told AFP. “The Houthi shell landed in the middle of the street, right in an area crowded with civilians.” Yemen’s government has announced a goal of retaking all Houthi territory — home to most of the country’s population, and much of it held for more than a decade. The humanitarian crisis caused by the war has left most of the nation’s population dependent on aid. Mohammed, a 33-year-old charity worker who fled from Mocha to Aden, told AFP on Tuesday that “people there are terrified” of the Houthis. AFP The post Saudi says three dead in airport attacks claimed by Houthis appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Impôts en Algérie : la déclaration des salaires devient obligatoire en ligne
items.description: De nouvelles dispositions sont applicables pour la déclaration fiscale des traitements et salaires par les entreprises en Algérie. Cette formalité, appelée G29 dans le jargon fiscal, doit désormais se faire en ligne. Une circulaire de la Direction générale des impôts (DGI), datée du 22 septembre dernier, a porté à la connaissance des services fiscaux l'obligation de la souscription de l'état des traitements et salaires par télédéclaration via la plateforme JIBAYATIC, conformément à l’article 8 de la loi de finances pour 2026 et à l'article 75 du code des impôts directs et taxes assimilées (CIDTA). La mesure est entrée en vigueur le 1ᵉʳ janvier 2026. La télédéclaration du G29 rendue obligatoire Les contribuables concernés sont ceux relevant des structures fiscales déjà dotées de ce système numérique, comme la Direction des grandes entreprises (DGE) et autres. Jusqu'alors, la souscription de la déclaration, au plus tard le 30 avril de chaque année, des traitements et émoluments divers payés pendant l'année précédente, pouvait s'effectuer par tous moyens, y compris sur support informatique ou par voie de télédéclaration, rappelle la DGI. Le mode d'accomplissement de cette déclaration était donc optionnel jusqu'au 31 décembre 2025. Désormais, la déclaration en ligne est obligatoire pour les contribuables relevant des services fiscaux dotés du système d'information JIBAYATIC. Cette mesure entre dans le cadre de la transformation numérique progressive de l’administration fiscale tendant, à la fois, à l'adaptation de ses services avec l'environnement et à l'amélioration de ses performances, notamment de la qualité des services, la simplification des procédures et la facilitation des démarches administratives, explique la direction des Impôts. Cela, tout en permettant à l’administration fiscale de disposer en temps réel des informations déclarées, qui sont « capitales pour l'exercice et l'accomplissement de ses missions et la préservation des intérêts du Trésor public ». Le numéro d’identification national de tous les salariés doit être intégré Désormais, le G29 doit être obligatoirement fourni dans le délai prévu par le CIDTA, par voie de télédéclaration, suivant le modèle d'imprimé prévu à cet effet par les contribuables relevant des services fiscaux dotés du système d'information JIBAYATIC. Le portail électronique dédié à cet effet sera incessamment mis en service, annonce la DGI. En cas de non-application des nouvelles dispositions, il sera procédé à l'application de la pénalité prévue par le CIDTA. Outre l'institution de l’obligation de la télédéclaration, la mesure dispose également que le numéro d'identification national unique (NIN) doit être intégré à l'état des salaires pour « chacun des bénéficiaires des paiements effectués », en plus des indications énumérées dans le CIDTA. Cela, explique la circulaire, en vue de se conformer aux dispositions du décret relatif au numéro d'identification national unique, qui constitue « un référentiel d'interopérabilité et d'échange d'informations avec les autres administrations et organismes publics, ce qui facilitera le traitement et l'exploitation des données et informations déclarées ». L’article Impôts en Algérie : la déclaration des salaires devient obligatoire en ligne est apparu en premier sur TSA .
